title: Corporate Governance Evidence from Strategic Emphasis: Evidence from India
summary: This study examines how corporate governance influences firms’ strategic emphasis following the adoption of takeover regulations in India. Specifically, it investigates whether a reduction in the threat of hostile takeovers affects the relative emphasis that firms place on short-term value appropriation and long-term value creation. Drawing on agency and stewardship perspectives, the study conceptualises advertising expenditure as an indicator of value appropriation and research and development (R&D) expenditure as an indicator of value creation. Using firm-level data from the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy Prowess database for Indian firms over the period 2000–2024, this study examines changes in advertising and R&D intensity following the 2011 takeover regulation reform. The analysis employs panel-data techniques, including dynamic estimation, to assess the relationship between takeover-law adoption and firms’ strategic emphasis while accounting for firm- and industry-level characteristics. The findings indicate that weakening the threat of a hostile takeover is associated with greater emphasis on value appropriation, as reflected in advertising expenditure, providing support for the managerial-entrenchment perspective. In contrast, the evidence does not provide consistent support for the shareholder-interest perspective that reduced takeover pressure would encourage greater investment in long-term value creation through R&D. The findings suggest that changes in the corporate control environment can influence how managers allocate resources between immediate market-oriented activities and longer-term investments. The study contributes to the corporate governance literature by providing evidence from an emerging-market context and by highlighting strategic emphasis as an important mechanism through which takeover regulation may shape managerial resource-allocation decisions.

title: Firm-Level Traits and Environmental Responsibility of Listed Industrial Goods Firms in Nigeria: Moderating Effect of Female Board Representation
summary: The study examined the moderating effect of female board representation on the relationship between firm-level traits and corporate environmental responsibility of listed industrial goods firms in Nigeria. The specific objectives were: to ascertain the moderating effect of female board representation on the relationship between firm leverage and environmental disclosure index; to determine the extent to which female board representation moderates the relationship between firm size and environmental disclosure index; to analyse the moderating effect of female board representation on the relationship between firm liquidity and environmental disclosure index. Ex-post facto research design was deployed. The study population comprised thirteen listed industrial goods firms in Nigeria. A sample size of nine was chosen. Secondary data were collected from the firms’ annual reports from 2012 to 2024. Analyses were first done using descriptive and correlational tools. Moderated panel regression was carried out to ascertain the nexus between firm-level traits and environmental responsibility. The hypotheses were tested using moderated panel regression analysis, which revealed that: female board representation has a negative and significant moderating effect on the effect of firm leverage on environmental disclosure (β = -0.1558; p = 0.0156); female board representation has a positive and significant moderating effect on the effect of firm size on environmental disclosure (β = 0.0440; p = 0.0000); female board representation has a negative and significant moderating effect on the effect of firm liquidity on environmental disclosure index of listed industrial goods firms in Nigeria (β = -0.1245; p = 0.0000). The study recommends that female board appointments should prioritize individuals with expertise in financial risk management and sustainability reporting to effectively mitigate the negative moderating effect of leverage on environmental disclosure.

title: Resiliencia empresarial, el arte de prosperar ante la incertidumbre
summary: A partir de la experiencia del sismo del 10 de agosto de 2026 en Colombia —que afectó gravemente a cerca de 270.000 empresas, compuestas en un 93% por microempresas—, se destaca la importancia de abordar la resiliencia no como un atributo pasivo, sino como una capacidad estratégica indispensable para la supervivencia y sostenibilidad del tejido productivo. El análisis demuestra la marcada vulnerabilidad de las mipymes ante eventos disruptivos y enfatiza la necesidad de articular procesos continuos de conocimiento, reducción del riesgo y manejo de desastres alineados con estándares internacionales como la norma ISO 22301 y la Ley 1523 de 2012. Para lograr una rápida recuperación y una transformación duradera, se requiere que las organizaciones implementen planes de continuidad de negocio probados mediante simulacros, cuenten con comités de crisis estructurados y aseguren el bienestar emocional de sus colaboradores como paso inicial. Asimismo, el texto concluye que la gran empresa debe liderar el fortalecimiento de sus cadenas de suministro transfiriendo capacidades a los pequeños proveedores, promoviendo el enfoque de reconstrucción Build Back Better e integrando la resiliencia dentro de los criterios de sostenibilidad y gobernanza corporativa.

title: Public and Private Capital’s Role in Advancing Green Finance Investment: Evidence from a Structural–behavioural Model of Capital Mobilisation in the UK
summary: Achieving net-zero targets requires the mobilisation of private capital alongside credible public policy support. This study examines how government support mechanisms shape green investment commitment among UK financial professionals through an integrated structural–behavioural model. The framework incorporates perceived government support, regulatory clarity, financial incentives, public capital availability, investor confidence, private capital mobilisation, and green investment commitment. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire using purposive sampling, yielding 187 valid responses from professionals involved in capital allocation, finance, sustainability, and related roles. Regression, simple mediation, serial mediation, and measurement-model diagnostics were used to evaluate the proposed relationships. The findings indicate that perceived government support and financial incentives are significant direct predictors of green investment commitment, while investor confidence functions as an important behavioural transmission mechanism. Regulatory clarity strengthens commitment indirectly through investor confidence. Public capital availability does not show a significant direct effect on green investment commitment; rather, its influence operates through private capital mobilisation, consistent with a crowding-in pathway. The serial mediation analysis further indicates that government support is most strongly associated with investor confidence when translated into credible financial incentives. Overall, the findings suggest that effective green finance mobilisation depends on policy credibility, regulatory clarity, well-designed incentives, and mechanisms that convert public support into confidence and private capital mobilisation.

title: Biodiversity Disclosure and Analyst Forecast Accuracy: Evidence From Chinese A‐Share Firms
summary: ABSTRACT We examine whether biodiversity‐related disclosure in annual reports is associated with analyst forecast accuracy among Chinese A‐share firms. Using 20,038 firm‐year observations from 2011 to 2023 and a dictionary‐based measure validated against independent manual coding, we find that greater disclosure intensity is associated with lower subsequent forecast error after accounting for firms' broader ESG and textual‐reporting characteristics. The negative association is evident in firm‐grouped cross‐fitted estimates and in forecasts issued within 30 days of annual‐report publication. Evidence for forecast dispersion is weaker.

title: When the storm hits: how does energy uncertainty influence green credit in Chinese banks?
summary: General economic policy uncertainty is known to suppress credit, yet the specific impact of energy-related uncertainty on sustainable finance remains underexplored. This study investigates the influence of the Energy Uncertainty Index (EUI) on Green Credit (GC) allocation within the Chinese banking sector. Using an unbalanced panel of 42 A-share-listed commercial banks from 2011 to 2023, we employ an import-share-weighted Geopolitical Risk (GPR) index as an instrumental variable and System GMM estimation to address endogeneity. Our results demonstrate that (i) heightened EUI prompts banks to structurally shift credit from carbon-intensive to green industries; (ii) panel quantile regression reveals that institutions with a stronger initial green credit base respond more vigorously to energy shocks; and (iii)the mechanism is robustly driven by a supply-side transmission channel—Peer Green Credit Pressure (PGCP)—while also providing empirical evidence consistent with a demand-side pull from corporate Green Investment Intensity (GI). Heterogeneity tests indicate this reallocation is most pronounced among state-owned banks, large-scale institutions, and banks in green finance pilot zones. These findings challenge the conventional view that uncertainty uniformly inhibits lending, illustrating instead that targeted energy uncertainty acts as a catalyst for green credit restructuring and enhances energy transition resilience.

title: Debt maturity structure, corporate governance, and hostile takeover threats: half a century of evidence
summary: Exploiting a takeover-threat measure that is less directly subject to managerial choice than firm-chosen governance provisions and a large sample spanning more than half a century, this study examines the association between hostile takeover threats and corporate debt maturity structure. Drawing on the hostile takeover index that has been widely used in the literature and a sample covering the period from 1964 to 2020, we investigate whether variation in takeover threats is associated with differences in firms’ debt maturity choices. We find that firms facing greater hostile takeover threats tend to rely more heavily on short-maturity debt, a pattern consistent with, although not demonstrating, the view that takeover threats and short-term debt may serve as complementary governance mechanisms that enhance outside monitoring and constrain managerial discretion. These associations remain robust across firm fixed-effects regressions, propensity score matching, entropy balancing, and instrumental-variable specifications. We also find that the association between takeover threats and shorter debt maturity is stronger among highly levered firms but weaker among firms with greater profitability, larger cash reserves, and higher capital expenditures. Because our design mitigates but does not eliminate endogeneity and alternative explanations, we interpret the evidence as a robust conditional association between hostile takeover threats and firms’ debt maturity policies rather than as causal evidence.

title: The underestimated emission reduction effect of green credit: a systematic study based on peer effects
summary: Against the backdrop of global efforts to address climate change and advance the low-carbon transition, green credit is widely regarded as a financial instrument that directs financial resources toward low-carbon activities. However, most existing studies focus on the direct effects of green credit on individual firms while overlooking interactions among firms. This study systematically examines the peer effects of green credit on corporate carbon reduction at the industry and city levels and explores the underlying mechanisms. To this end, a theoretical model is developed to explain how green credit induces peer effects on corporate carbon reduction. The theoretical predictions are then tested using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms. The results show that greater access to green credit among peer firms significantly reduces the carbon emission intensity of focal firms, indicating that green credit generates carbon-reduction peer effects at both the industry and city levels. Market competition and learning and imitation are important mechanisms through which these peer effects operate. The carbon-reduction peer effects of green credit are more pronounced among firms in industries not subject to green-credit restrictions and among those located in Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zones. This study advances theoretical modeling and empirical research on green finance and corporate peer effects and provides useful evidence for policymakers seeking to reassess the emission-reduction effects of green credit policies.

title: The Influence of Sustainable Finance and Corporate Governance on Investment Performance via Risk Management Effectiveness in the Banking Industry
summary: This study examined the associations of sustainable finance and corporate governance with investment performance, both directly and indirectly through risk management effectiveness, among managers of KBMI 3 and KBMI 4 banks operating in Jakarta, Indonesia. Using an explanatory quantitative survey, data were collected from 250 purposively selected managerial respondents through four-point Likert-scale questionnaires and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The reported results showed positive associations of sustainable finance and corporate governance with risk management effectiveness and of risk management effectiveness with investment performance. Corporate governance was also directly associated with investment performance, whereas the direct sustainable finance–investment performance relationship was not statistically significant. Both specified indirect associations through risk management effectiveness were reported as significant. These findings suggest that risk management practices may be an important organizational pathway linking sustainability and governance arrangements with perceived investment performance. Because the data are questionnaire-based and the reported structural coefficients require reconciliation with the original analysis output, the results should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causal effects.

title: Release or Squeeze? The Impact of the Digital Economy on Vegetation Cover in Chinese Cities
summary: Whether digitalization, while promoting urban economic growth, is accompanied by environmental problems is crucial for a comprehensive understanding of the sustainability of the digital economy. Using remote sensing–based ecological data for 284 Chinese cities from 2003 to 2023, this study identifies the effect of digital economy development on vegetation dynamics through a double machine learning framework. The main findings are as follows: (1) a one-standard-deviation increase in the digital economy index reduces city-level vegetation cover by approximately 1.13%. (2) The mechanism operates through a dominance of agglomeration costs over efficiency gains induced by digitalization, manifested in intensified land development and increased air pollution, ultimately encroaching upon green space. (3) Further analysis shows that digital economy-induced vegetation degradation follows an inverted-U-shaped pattern as population density increases, and this adverse impact also exhibits a pronounced spatial spillover to neighboring cities. These findings suggest that digitalization entails a trade-off between efficiency gains and agglomeration costs, underscoring the need for urban management policies that balance digital growth and ecological sustainability.

title: A Study on the Relationship Between the Digital Economy, Industrial Relocation, and Labor Migration
summary: Digitalized economy has been revamping the world industrial division of labor together with driving industrial relocation by geographical relocation of industries into digital restructuring of industries chains. Being one of the main factors influencing the process of industrial relocation, labor migration will undergo significant change in the patterns and determinants of migration. It is evident that digital tech alters the spatial logic of labor migration by reducing the cost of information and transactions as well as industrial relocations keep moving the regional labor force overtime due to the creation of job opportunities and the shifting nature of skill demands. The research suggests that the results of this study would help to enhance the digital infrastructure in the interior areas and improve the policies on talents in order to bring in skilled employees. Meanwhile, firms should embrace remote-work models to reduce unnecessary geographic moves. Crucially, targeted digital training is needed for low-skilled migrants, so they are not left behind. The present analysis offers empirical support to the concept that there are new features and processes of migration in a digital economy environment, offering a reference for formulating regional coordinated development strategies and labor market policies.

title: Government digital transformation and high-quality economic development: evidence from chinese listed enterprises
summary: Unlike prior studies that examine government digital transformation (GDT) primarily from governmental or macroeconomic perspectives, this study investigates the effect of GDT on economic output from the perspective of enterprises. This paper treats the establishment of integrated government service platforms as an institutional shock representing GDT and constructs a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) model to estimate the effect of GDT on high-quality economic development. Empirical results suggest that GDT significantly promotes high-quality economic development, and these results remain robust across a series of robustness tests, including PSM-DID estimation, exclusion of regional self-selection and contemporaneous policy shocks, alternative fixed-effects specifications, and variable substitutions. This study also identifies those conditions under which GDT promotes high-quality economic development by examining the key dimensions of government behavior. Results indicate that strong fiscal support constitutes a critical foundation for effective GDT, lower fiscal transparency amplifies the marginal impact of GDT on high-quality economic development, and stronger digital leadership capacity further strengthens these positive effects. Enterprise digitalization also exhibits a complementary relationship with GDT, with the latter exhibiting stronger inclusive effects. Aside from offering theoretical support to achieve a balance between “effective government” and “efficient markets” in developing economies with complex institutional environments and pronounced regional disparities, these results offer important policy implications for governments seeking to overcome governance bottlenecks and fully realize the dividends of digital transformation.

title: CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY (CSR) DALAM KAITANNYA DENGAN PELESTARIAN LINGKUNGAN DAN MASYARAKAT WILAYAH PESISIR DAN PULAU-PULAU KECIL DI INDONESIA
summary: Wilayah pesisir dan pulau-pulau kecil di Indonesia memiliki potensi sumber daya alam yang melimpah, namun sekaligus sangat rentan terhadap degradasi lingkungan dan masalah ketimpangan sosial-ekonomi. Kehadiran berbagai aktivitas industri dan korporasi di sekitar kawasan ini membawa dampak ekologis dan sosial yang signifikan, sehingga menuntut optimalisasi pelaksanaan Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji dan menganalisis implementasi program CSR dalam kaitannya dengan pelestarian lingkungan serta pemberdayaan masyarakat di kawasan pesisir dan pulau-pulau kecil Indonesia. Melalui metode kualitatif dengan pendekatan studi literatur dan analisis deskriptif, penelitian ini mengevaluasi berbagai praktik CSR yang telah berjalan. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar implementasi CSR di wilayah ini masih cenderung bersifat karitatif (bantuan sesaat) dan belum sepenuhnya berorientasi pada keberlanjutan. Tantangan utama yang dihadapi meliputi minimnya partisipasi masyarakat lokal dalam perencanaan, ketidaksesuaian program dengan karakteristik geografis pulau kecil, serta kurangnya sinergi dengan pemerintah daerah. Program CSR dinilai efektif apabila mengintegrasikan kearifan lokal dan pendekatan ekonomi sirkular, seperti program rehabilitasi ekosistem mangrove, budidaya perikanan berkelanjutan, dan pengembangan ekowisata. Disimpulkan bahwa CSR di wilayah pesisir dan pulau-pulau kecil harus bertransformasi dari kewajiban filantropis menjadi strategi penciptaan nilai bersama (Creating Shared Value). Diperlukan kolaborasi sinergis antara perusahaan, pemerintah, dan masyarakat untuk mewujudkan kelestarian ekologi pesisir yang selaras dengan peningkatan kesejahteraan nelayan dan penduduk setempat.

title: Innovative Practices and Development Countermeasures of Enterprise Human Capital Management in the Era of Digital Economy
summary: The digital economy is profoundly and comprehensively reshaping the underlying logic and operational paradigm of enterprise human capital management. The large-scale and increasingly widespread application of data as a core production factor is driving management decision-making away from experience-based judgment and toward scientific prediction and evidence-based forecasting. As a result, the functional positioning, operating mechanisms, and value creation approaches of human capital management are all facing systematic reconstruction and fundamental transformation. Grounded in the context of the digital economy era, this paper systematically analyzes the internal mechanism through which enterprise human capital management transitions from “personnel and administrative affairs management” to “data-driven value operation and management.” It reviews and organizes corporate innovation practice pathways from four dimensions: data-driven decision-making, intelligent talent allocation and deployment, digital training and development systems, and flexible incentive and assessment mechanisms. In addition, by incorporating industry survey data, the paper reveals the key bottlenecks currently encountered in this transformation, including weak data governance, organizational inertia and resistance, and the digital capability gap among talent. On this basis, the paper proposes development countermeasures from four aspects: consolidating the foundation of data governance, promoting the reconstruction of organizational capabilities, cultivating compound and interdisciplinary digital talent, and establishing a dynamic evaluation mechanism. The aim is to provide theoretical reference and practical guidance for enterprises seeking to achieve a leap in human capital management from control to empowerment, and from functional orientation to value creation.

title: ESG performance under concentrated ownership: a principal–principal agency perspective
summary: The study examines the effect of ownership concentration on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance in emerging markets affected by principal-principal agency conflicts. Using a panel of 1,842 firm-year observations from listed firms in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines during 2013 to 2021, the analysis measures ESG performance through composite and pillar-level scores from S&P Capital IQ Pro and captures ownership concentration through the equity stake held by the largest shareholder. After controlling for firm characteristics, macroeconomic conditions, industry fixed effects, and year fixed effects, the results reveal a strong negative association between ownership concentration and overall ESG performance. Concentrated ownership appears less willing to support ESG initiatives, potentially treating them as costly commitments that reduce the benefits of private control and divert resources from controlling shareholders. Pillar-level analysis indicates dimension-level heterogeneity in the association between ownership concentration and ESG performance. Ownership concentration is negatively associated with environmental, social, and governance performance, with the governance pillar showing the largest and most statistically significant estimated association. The study extends principal-principal agency theory into sustainability research and yields practical implications for regulators, investors, and policymakers in concentrated-ownership settings.

title: The Strategic Implementation of Digital Transformation at Perumda Tirta Pakuan Bogor
summary: Background: In 2021, the PERUMDA Tirta Pakuan Bogor initiated a digital transformation program with the primary objective of improving operational efficiency and enhancing customer service. However, after four years of implementation, the transformation has yet to show significant impact, as evidenced by increasing annual expenditures and the company’s continued failure to achieve targeted water supply continuity.Purpose: This study aims to identify the key factors influencing the implementation of digital transformation at PERUMDA Tirta Pakuan and formulate strategic recommendations to strengthen this implementation. By understanding these driving factors, organizations can enhance their operational performance and service delivery.Design/methodology/approach: This research employed a non-probability sampling method, gathering valid responses from 200 employees and 4 expert informants. Structural equation modeling–partial least squares (SEM-PLS) was used to test hypotheses and evaluate the complex relationships among variables. In addition, the analytical hierarchy process (AHP) was applied to develop a prioritized strategy to support digital transformation initiatives.Findings/Results: The findings reveal that organizational culture, resources, and technology have a positive and significant influence on the implementation of digital transformation. Furthermore, among the indirect effects tested, only organizational culture significantly influences digital transformation implementation through the mediating variable of digital transformation acceptance attitude. The strategic analysis using AHP indicates that resources are the top priority factor in supporting digital transformation. Consequently, the most recommended strategy is the optimization of the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, as it is considered capable of enhancing productivity, efficiency, service quality, and overall performance growth.Conclusion: This study highlights the importance of organizational culture and resources in enabling successful digital transformation, with culture playing a mediating role in shaping attitudes toward change. The strategic prioritization of SCADA system optimization is essential to maximize the benefits of digital initiatives.Originality/value (State of the art): This study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on public sector digital transformation by offering empirical insights into the interrelationships among organizational culture, resources, technology, and transformation success. It also provides strategic recommendations using a hybrid SEM-PLS and AHP approach, offering practical value to public utilities aiming to modernize their operations Keywords: digital transformation, organizational culture, technology, public utilities, SCADA system

title: Innovation financière, FinTech et politique monétaire : Cartographie de la recherche scientifique
summary: Résumé : L’essor de l’innovation financière et de la FinTech transforme les mécanismes d’intermédiation, les moyens de paiement et les comportements monétaires, soulevant de nouvelles interrogations sur la demande de monnaie et la transmission de la politique monétaire. Malgré l’essor de ces travaux, la littérature bibliométrique existante reste principalement centrée sur l’innovation financière ou sur la FinTech, sans proposer une cartographie intégrée de l’intersection entre innovation financière, FinTech, demande de monnaie et politique monétaire, notamment en prolongement des travaux de Metwalli et al. (2025b). Dans ce contexte, la question de recherche est la suivante : comment la recherche scientifique sur l’innovation financière, la FinTech, la demande de monnaie et la politique monétaire s’est-elle structurée entre 2000 et 2024 ? L’étude vise à identifier les principales caractéristiques de la production scientifique, les acteurs et réseaux de collaboration ainsi que les principales structures thématiques de ce champ. Elle repose sur une analyse bibliométrique des publications indexées dans Scopus. La recherche, effectuée le 2 mars 2026, utilise une requête TITLE-ABS-KEY combinant « financial innovation » ou « fintech » avec « monetary policy » ou « money demand », et retient les articles en anglais relevant du domaine Economics, publiés au stade final entre 2000 et 2024. L’année 2025 n’a pas été intégrée afin de conserver une dernière année complète et stabilisée dans le périmètre temporel défini par le protocole de recherche. Sur les 263 documents initialement identifiés, 111 articles ont été retenus. Les États-Unis constituent le principal contributeur avec 26 publications, suivis du Royaume-Uni avec 18 et de la Chine avec 14. La cartographie VOSviewer du réseau de co-occurrence fait ressortir 18 mots-clés répartis en 5 clusters, reliés par 57 liens pour une force totale de liens de 117. Les résultats mettent ainsi en évidence une structuration du champ autour de la demande de monnaie et de la politique monétaire, de l’innovation financière et de la FinTech, de l’inclusion financière ainsi que des nouvelles formes monétaires numériques, notamment les cryptomonnaies et les CBDC. Cette cartographie permet de mieux caractériser la structure scientifique du domaine et d’identifier des perspectives de recherche à l’intersection de la transformation numérique, des comportements monétaires et de la transmission de la politique monétaire. Mots clés : Innovation financière, FinTech, politique monétaire, demande de monnaie, inclusion financière, CBDC, bibliométrie, science mapping, Scopus, VOSviewer. JEL Classification : E41 ; E42 ; E52 ; E58 ; G20 ; G23 ; O33. Type du papier : Recherche empirique : analyse bibliométrique. Abstract: The expansion of financial innovation and FinTech is transforming financial intermediation, payment systems, and monetary behavior, raising new questions about money demand and monetary policy transmission. Despite the growing body of research, existing bibliometric studies remain largely focused on financial innovation or FinTech separately and do not provide an integrated mapping of the intersection between financial innovation, FinTech, money demand, and monetary policy, particularly in relation to the contribution of Metwalli et al. (2025b). Against this background, the research question is: how has scientific research on financial innovation, FinTech, money demand, and monetary policy been structured between 2000 and 2024? The study aims to identify the main characteristics of scientific production, collaboration networks, and thematic structures within this field. A bibliometric analysis is conducted using publications indexed in Scopus. The search, performed on March 2, 2026, uses a TITLE-ABS-KEY query combining financial innovation or fintech with monetary policy or money demand and considers English-language articles classified under Economics and published at the final stage between 2000 and 2024. The year 2025 was excluded in order to maintain a complete and stabilized final year within the temporal scope defined by the research protocol. Of the 263 documents initially identified, 111 articles were retained. The United States is the leading contributor with 26 publications, followed by the United Kingdom with 18 and China with 14. VOSviewer co-occurrence mapping identifies 18 keywords grouped into 5 clusters, with 57 links and a total link strength of 117. The results reveal a research structure centered on money demand and monetary policy, financial innovation and FinTech, financial inclusion, and emerging digital monetary forms, particularly cryptocurrencies and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs). The mapping provides a clearer characterization of the scientific structure of the field and identifies avenues for future research at the intersection of digital transformation, monetary behavior, and monetary policy transmission. title: Managing change in the era of digital transformation. The case of Greek public sector
summary: Purpose This study examines the crucial process of implementing digital transformation in the Greek public sector, investigating how organizational framework, organizational sustainment, and employee digital readiness influence the successful integration of technological changes and digital reforms. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted with 233 Greek civil servants attending undergraduate and postgraduate programs in Public Administration. The study employed validated measurement scales including Holt et al.'s (2007) Readiness for Organizational Change scale, Miller's (1997) Integration of Change scale, and Westerman et al.'s (2014) scales for Organizational Frame and Sustainment of Digital Challenge. Data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis, Cronbach's alpha coefficients, Pearson correlations, multiple regression models, and bootstrapped mediation analysis via Hayes' (2022) PROCESS macro (Model 4, 5,000 resamples) to test hypotheses regarding direct and indirect effects. Findings Results demonstrate that organizational frame of digital challenge and organizational sustainment of digital transformation significantly and positively affect both employee readiness for digital change and successful integration of digital initiatives. Employee readiness partially mediates the relationships between organizational conditions (framing and sustainment) and integration success, explaining the mechanisms through which organizational interventions translate into successful outcomes. Originality/value This research fills a crucial gap by comprehensively examining relationships between digital organizational frame, sustainment, readiness, and their combined effect on implementation success. It validates Westerman et al.'s digital transformation compass in public sector contexts and provides empirical evidence for developing best practices in digital transformation management for public organizations.

title: Blind Box Cultural Marketing Strategies in the Digital Economy: A Case Study of POP MART
summary: Digital platforms have changed how people search for products, talk about brands and share their purchases. In the trendy toy market, this change is especially visible because buying a figure can involve character stories, online discussion and offline experience at the same time. This study examines POP MART as a case of blind box cultural marketing in the digital economy. A qualitative case study and literature analysis are used, drawing on academic research, POP MART's 2025 annual report and documented marketing practices. The analysis focuses on three dimensions: cultural marketing and brand value, digital platforms and consumer participation, and blind box consumption experience and brand loyalty. The findings suggest that POP MART builds value through character IP, keeps these characters visible through digital content and consumer sharing, and extends the blind box experience through collecting, communities and physical spaces. Although the blind box remains important, long term IP development and cultural adaptation appear more important for the future of the brand. The case may also be useful for other cultural consumption brands trying to build lasting consumer relationships.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Strategic Management and Corporate Governance in Selected Tertiary Institutions in Imo State, Nigeria
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a prevailing tool for driving strategic management and corporate governance of tertiary institutions in Nigeria, with the goal of transiting the quality of education from its current state to a desired future state. This study adopted the correlational survey research design and it was carried out in some selected tertiary institutions in Imo State, Nigeria with 200purposefully sampled respondents comprising of 100 senior and 100 junior administrative staff of the selected Public Teriary Institutions. The data for this study were collected via two researcher made rating scales. The first is titled Artificial Intelligence and Strategic Management Questionnaire (AISMQ) and the second is Artificial Intelligence and Corporate Governance Questionnaire (AICGQ) which were reviewed and validated by three experts in relevant academic fields such as computer science, educational administration, planning, measurement and evaluation. The reliability was established using the test–retest method, and the scores were correlated using Pearson’s Product Moment Correlation Coefficient, yielding reliability indices of 0.88 and 0.87, confirming high instrument reliability. The data were analyzed using the Pearson’s correlation at a 0.05 level of significance and the results revealed a significant relation between artificial intelligence and strategic management and corporate governance respectively. The paper concluded that artificial intelligence offers Nigerian tertiary institutions a practical means of strengthening strategic management and corporate governance by converting fragmented institutional data into timely insight, improving decision-making, and enhancing oversight .It further recommended that university management and governing councils should use AI outputs to inform strategic decisions while maintaining collegial deliberation and professional oversight. This preserves academic autonomy and contextual judgment that algorithms cannot replicate.

title: Leading Digital Transformation in Salaf Islamic Education: Negotiating Technology and Tradition
summary: Digital transformation in Salafi Islamic education presents leadership challenges, as the use of technology must be aligned with the traditions and institutional identity of the pesantren. This study aims to analyse how leaders navigate digital transformation within the context of Salafi Islamic education. The research employs a qualitative approach using a case study design at the Al-Anshoriyah Islamic Boarding School. Data were collected through interviews with three key informants the pesantren director, the chair of the board of trustees, and the headteacher as well as through observation and documentation. The data were analysed thematically by comparing information from the three data collection methods. The research findings identified three interrelated leadership practices: the selective adoption of technology, the gradual management of organisational change, and the negotiation between the utilisation of technology and the continuity of Salaf traditions. Key findings indicate that the continuity of traditional practices does not necessarily signify resistance to digitalisation, but can form part of leadership considerations in determining the scope of technological change. This study offers a perspective on ‘tradition-sensitive digital leadership’, which emphasises the role of leaders in aligning the use of technology with the identity and educational commitments of Islamic boarding schools. This perspective provides a contextual foundation for understanding digital transformation in Islamic educational institutions that uphold their institutional traditions.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION ON ORGANISATIONAL PERFORMANCE IN SELECTED DEPOSIT MONEY BANKS IN ABEOKUTA, OGUN STATE, NIGERIA
summary: The study investigates the impact of digital transformation on organizational performance within selected deposit money banks in Abeokuta, Ogun State, Nigeria. The research aims to analyze how IT infrastructure, digital skills, and automation influence operational efficiency, customer patronage, and profitability in this sector. Utilizing a descriptive survey research design, primary data was collected through structured questionnaires administered to employees across four banks, selected to represent a diverse workforce. A total of 141 respondents were sampled using a proportionate stratified random sampling technique to ensure an unbiased representation. The analysis revealed significant findings: IT infrastructure explains 73.3% of the variation in operational efficiency, digital skills account for 71.0% of the variation in customer patronage, and automation impacts profitability by 69.1%. Each hypothesis was tested using regression analysis, leading to the rejection of the null hypotheses, indicating that IT infrastructure, digital skills, and automation all positively influence the respective performance outcomes. The findings underscore the critical role of digital transformation in the banking sector, suggesting that continuous investment in technology infrastructure, employee digital competency training, and expanded automation practices are essential for enhancing operational efficiency, customer service, and overall profitability. This research contributes to the understanding of how digital innovations can drive performance in the Nigerian banking landscape and offers practical recommendations for banks to thrive in an increasingly digital marketplace.

title: Digital transformation and workforce resilience in social enterprises: governance for crisis readiness
summary: Purpose This study examines how digital transformation, workforce resilience and governance integration influence crisis readiness in social enterprises. It explores capability-building as a potential mechanism connecting digital transformation and governance with crisis readiness, while governance maturity and ecosystem collaboration are considered contextual conditions that may shape these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative design combined a comprehensive literature review of forty peer-reviewed studies with six semi-structured interviews involving governance, workforce and digital transformation leaders. Inductive coding identified three themes: governance for crisis readiness, digital transformation enablers and workforce resilience routines, interpreted through institutional theory and dynamic capability theory. Findings Governance embedded in digital workflows strengthens reliability and accountability. Capability-building routines such as micro-drills, peer learning, and digital literacy translate strategy into continuity outcomes. Ecosystem partnerships and institutional maturity amplify these effects by improving interoperability, resource sharing and collective learning. Practical implications Integrating governance controls within digital systems and aligning workforce development with feedback and monitoring enhances readiness, transparency and long-term sustainability. Originality/value This study develops a mechanism-informed conceptual framework that integrates governance maturity, digital transformation and workforce capability to explain potential pathways toward crisis readiness in social enterprises. It identifies capability-building as a proposed explanatory mechanism and ecosystem conditions as contextual influences, offering an integrative foundation for future empirical testing.

title: Classified boards, unclassified outcomes: a focused survey of non-financial evidence
summary: This review examines how classified (staggered) boards affect non-financial corporate outcomes and how these outcomes inform the long-standing debate over the value of takeover defenses. We develop a framework based on four competing perspectives: the entrenchment view, the bonding hypothesis, the myopic-markets hypothesis, and the optimal-governance view. These perspectives generate distinct predictions for outcomes that are often obscured by aggregate financial measures such as Tobin’s Q and stock returns. We review evidence on innovation, environmental performance, labor investment, corporate social responsibility, corporate culture, inclusion-related policies, and voting premiums, which we treat as direct evidence on managerial entrenchment rather than as a conventional non-financial outcome. The evidence suggests that staggered boards can promote innovation and labor-related outcomes by supporting long-term investment and stakeholder commitment, while also imposing costs in areas such as corporate culture, social capital and corporate social responsibility, inclusion, and private-benefit extraction. Environmental findings remain mixed. Our primary contribution is a mechanism-based synthesis that clarifies when, why, and for which stakeholders staggered boards are likely to create benefits or costs.

title: ІННОВАЦІЙНІ ІНСТРУМЕНТИ РОЗВИТКУ ФОНДОВОГО РИНКУ
summary: The article is devoted to the study of modern innovative instruments of the stock market and their definition. The study determined the role of digital financial instruments in the transformation of the mechanisms of capital markets. The main trends in the development of financial technologies were considered. Their impact on increasing the efficiency of investment activities, optimizing asset management and ensuring the transparency of stock market transactions was analyzed. The advantages of using innovative instruments compared to traditional approaches to investment were determined. The main advantages are high speed of transactions, reduced transaction costs, expanded access to financial services, automation of decision-making processes and increased liquidity of capital markets. The article examines the features of the application of blockchain technologies, tokenization of financial assets, cryptocurrencies, exchange-traded funds for digital assets and digital currencies of central banks. Smart contracts, fintech platforms, open banking solutions and APIs are considered. Special attention is paid to Big Data technologies, artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotic process automation, algorithmic and high-frequency trading, robo-advisory as an innovative tool for managing investment portfolios. The global experience of using innovative stock market instruments is analyzed. Current trends in their development on leading international stock exchanges are identified. Particular attention is paid to the risks and challenges associated with the implementation of new technologies. These include cyber risks, regulatory restrictions, technological risks, volatility of digital assets and information protection problems. It is substantiated that the further implementation of innovative instruments will contribute to increasing the efficiency of the stock market. This will ensure its competitiveness, expand investment opportunities and contribute to the formation of a modern digital financial ecosystem.

title: Digitalising what Matters: Digital Transformation and Shifting Orders of Worth in Public Transport
summary: Abstract Digital transformation does more than change how public organisations work. It transforms what they consider worth pursuing in the first place. This article examines how digitalization reconfigures the values, expertise, and justificatory principles that underpin public services. Drawing on four years of qualitative fieldwork in the Swedish public transport sector, we show that a Public Transport Authority’s shift from procuring off-the-shelf digital solutions to developing in-house digital capabilities involved the recruitment of new professional groups, the adoption of new work methods, and the display of new forms of expertise. As a result, creativity, experimentation, user-centredness, and innovation became principles for evaluating and justifying organisational practices and decisions alongside established public-value principles of efficiency, equality, and collective responsibility. These changes extended beyond organisational boundaries, as new practices and justificatory principles began to circulate and were invoked by various actors across the broader field of public transport. Our conceptual contribution lies in articulating this process as world transgression: a field-level process through which principles of worth associated with one justificatory world enter and gain legitimacy within worlds historically organised around others. Taken together, these results contribute to ongoing debates on digitalization and field-level transformations by showing that the adoption of new technologies and organisational structures comes with the emergence of new modes of thought, such as design thinking, new forms of expertise and, not least, new ways of justifying organisational practices and decisions.

title: INTERNATIONAL PRACTICE OF CORPORATE FINANCE ORGANIZATION: FINANCING STRUCTURE, CORPORATE GOVERNANCE REFORMS AND STATE ASSET MANAGEMENT EXPERIENCE
summary: The article provides a comparative analysis of how corporate finance is organized in developed and emerging economies and draws practical lessons for Uzbekistan. The aim of the study is to identify which elements of foreign practice in the areas of corporate financing structure, corporate governance and state asset management are suitable for national conditions. The methodology combines comparative institutional analysis, analysis of World Bank statistical data and case studies. The sample includes the USA, Germany, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. The results reveal substantial differences in the structure of national financial systems. In the USA, stock market capitalization exceeds domestic credit to the private sector by 1.17 times, whereas this ratio is 0.74 in Germany and 0.49 in Uzbekistan. In Uzbekistan, domestic credit to the private sector amounts to 32.8% of GDP and market capitalization to 16.1% of GDP, indicating that corporate financing is constrained through both the bank and the market channels. Among recent foreign reforms, the initiative on management conscious of the cost of capital and stock price launched in Japan in 2023 stands out: more than 90% of Prime Market companies have disclosed relevant plans, and their average P/B ratio has increased from 1.1 to 1.4. South Korea's 2024 Value-up programme follows the same logic. Kazakhstan's People's IPO and Singapore's Temasek model are shown to be effective ways of subjecting state assets to market discipline. At the same time, because stock market liquidity in Uzbekistan is low and most shares are owned by the state, exchange-led initiatives need to be combined with the state's requirements as an owner. The article proposes forming a mixed financing model, transferring state-owned enterprises to professional management, introducing cost-of-capital-oriented disclosure requirements and clearly defining dividend policy in legislation.

title: Geography-Based Funding and the Fintech Securities Crowdfunding Ecosystem in Indonesia: A Mixed-Method Analysis
summary: Background: The Fintech Securities Crowdfunding (SCF) industry in Indonesia has shown rapid growth, yet it faces challenges regarding the uneven distribution of funding access and the maturity of its ecosystem. While funding is a primary driver, the geographical dimension in an archipelago nation remains a critical, under-researched variable. Objective: This study aims to analyze the influence of Funding on the Fintech SCF Ecosystem and examine the mediating role of Geography in this relationship. Methods: This research employs a mixed-method approach. The quantitative phase utilizes Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) to analyze data from SCF investors. The qualitative phase employs Social Network Analysis (SNA) to map the relationships among ecosystem actors. Results: Quantitative results indicate that Funding has a significant positive effect on the SCF Ecosystem (t-statistic 2.938). Crucially, Geography significantly mediates this relationship (t-statistic 2.269), suggesting that funding effectiveness relies on spatial distribution. SNA results visualize the central role of platforms in bridging geographical gaps between issuers and investors. Conclusion: A robust SCF ecosystem depends not only on capital volume but on how funding strategies address geographical disparities. This study integrates the functional area of funding with geographical disparity theories within the Fintech Ecosystem framework, offering a novel perspective on "hyper-local" strategies for national inclusivity.

title: Human Capital in AI-Enabled Digital Transformation: A Systematic Review of Workforce Competencies and HRM Mechanisms
summary: This article presents a systematic literature review of the role of human capital in digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on how these developments reshape workforce competencies and human resource management (HRM) during the transition from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0. Following the PRISMA guidelines, the study combines thematic coding with comparative analysis. From an initial pool of 216 publications, 46 studies were selected for in-depth analysis. The review examines how AI and digitalisation change workforce skill requirements and how HRM mechanisms can help organisations develop and sustain the necessary competencies. The findings indicate a shift from routine and manual tasks toward hybrid competency profiles that integrate data analytics skills, AI literacy, human–machine interaction skills, and higher-order socio-cognitive capabilities, including adaptive reasoning, collaboration, and ethical judgement. HRM emerges as a strategic integrator that supports continuous reskilling, predictive skills-gap analysis, and the development of effective human–AI teams. Based on these findings, the study proposes a multilevel framework explaining how institutional mechanisms, organisational strategy, HRM practices, and human–AI complementarity jointly shape workforce competitiveness in AI-enabled digital transformation. The framework contributes to human-centric digitalisation by linking workforce competitiveness to capability velocity and human–AI complementarity. It also provides managerial implications for designing learning, governance, and decision-making structures that enable organisations to respond to evolving competency requirements and translate technological potential into sustainable operational advantages.

title: Systematic Literature Review: Pengaruh Manajemen Operasi Bisnis terhadap Kinerja Organisasi Bisnis di Indonesia
summary: This systematic literature review examines the impact of business operations management on organizational business performance in Indonesia during 2015-2025. From 37 peer-reviewed articles analyzed using qualitative and quantitative approaches, research findings demonstrate that business operations management, particularly supply chain management, quality management, and digital transformation, significantly influence organizational performance in Indonesia across operational, financial, and strategic dimensions. The study identifies competitive advantage, organizational innovation, and supply chain integration as strong mediating variables in the relationship between operations management practices and organizational performance. Additionally, the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies such as IoT, artificial intelligence, and big data analytics shows substantial positive impacts on operational efficiency. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the mechanisms through which business operations management enhances organizational performance in the Indonesian and ASEAN context. Practical implications include recommendations for managers and policymakers to integrate sustainable operations management practices with digital technology investments to achieve long-term competitive advantage.

title: ECONOMIC AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF CONSTRUCTION ENTERPRISES IN THE CONTEXT OF DEVELOPING ADAPTIVE MECHANISMS FOR STRATEGIC DEVELOPMENT
summary: Transformational changes in construction enterprises are increasingly linked to the integration of digital technologies into the economic management system and to the need for new mechanisms of adaptation. The purpose of the article is to determine the conditions under which the intensity of digital restructuring of a construction enterprise is converted into economic performance growth, and to substantiate the conceptual and mathematical foundations for choosing an adaptive trajectory of strategic development. Digital restructuring covers not only technological modernization but also a change in the ways of using economic potential, organizing information interaction and making managerial decisions. Economic and digital transformation is considered as a coordinated reconfiguration of an enterprise's internal structure, within which digital and technological integration, information synchronization, economic manageability, process flexibility and managerial adaptability form an interconnected system of strategic transformations. The study applies systemic, structural-parametric and risk-oriented approaches, structural decomposition, normalization, weighted aggregation, non-linear modelling and trajectory analysis. A system of indicators is proposed: a composite index of digital restructuring, coefficients of structural synchronization and inter-circuit balance, indicators of transformational effectiveness, capacity and risk-adjusted stability, and an integrated trajectory function. Calculations show that a high weighted average level of components is accompanied by lower structural synchronization and inter-circuit balance, caused by the lag of the process-adaptation circuit behind the digital-integration one. Four modes of strategic behaviour are identified: stabilization, adaptive build-up, accelerated transformation and advanced development; the transition between them is formalized through the ratio of transformational capacity, impulse intensity, structural synchronization and risk load. The effectiveness of transformation depends on the proportional development of components rather than on maximizing individual ones.

title: Sustainability-benefit beliefs, Generation Z’s intentions and actual use of financial technology university students in Indonesia
summary: Recent literature linking pro-FinTech and ecological awareness that supports sustainable performance emphasizes the perspective of corporations as FinTech service providers. This study provides empirical evidence of the relationship between sustainability-benefit beliefs and pro-FinTech behavior. In the user context, pro-fintech is the behavioral intention to use FinTech. The research data comprised 319 Generation Z students in Indonesia. The data were analyzed using SEM-PLS. This study reports that sustainability-benefit beliefs increase behavioral intention to use FinTech. We separate sustainability-benefit beliefs into economic, environmental, and social categories and find that both environmental and economic-benefit beliefs positively affect behavioral intention to use FinTech. However, social-benefit belief does not influence behavioral intention to use FinTech. This study is beneficial for users and financial institutions in increasing the number of FinTech users. FinTech service developers are advised to innovate to develop solutions that continuously improve perceived sustainability performance. Financial institutions are advised to raise public awareness of FinTech’s benefits, as this is essential to fostering a positive perception of FinTech’s ability to improve perceived sustainability performance.

title: THE ROLE OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT IN ATTRACTING FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT IN EMERGING MARKETS

title: How Does Green Finance Policy Promote City Green Growth? The Roles of Green Innovation and Entrepreneurship
summary: Although green finance policies are widely recognized as important instruments for promoting city green growth, how they reshape the behavioral responses of economic actors remains insufficiently understood. This study examines green innovation and entrepreneurship within a common analytical framework, with the former representing a technological response and the latter a market-entry response. Drawing on a panel of 282 Chinese prefecture-level cities over 2011–2022, this study exploits the implementation of the Pilot Zone for Green Finance Reform and Innovation (PZGFRI) policy as a quasi-natural experiment and estimates its effect on green total factor productivity using a difference-in-differences design. The baseline estimate is 0.168, implying an effect equivalent to about 15.7% of the sample mean of GTFP, and this result is broadly comparable across robustness checks. The mechanism analyses further show positive policy effects on green innovation and entrepreneurial entry, with both lagged measures positively associated with subsequent city GTFP. Heterogeneity analyses suggest that policy effects are more pronounced in peripheral cities, cities with lower government efficiency, and those with lower pollution pressure. The results imply that green finance should be more precisely targeted, stimulate both technological and market-entry responses, and be adapted to local development conditions. These insights may also be relevant to developing economies seeking to turn policy-based financial support into sustained green growth.

Detailed description of the research paper Research title Research title The AI Tsunami: Transforming Employment, Skills, and the Future of Work in the Digital Economy Subtitle: An Integrated Analysis of Automation, Human–AI Collaboration, Workforce Reskilling, and Socioeconomic Transformation Author: Geruganti SudhakarAffiliation: Faculty, IIIT RGUKT Basar Background and rationale Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming an important component of the modern economy, influencing how businesses operate, how professionals perform their duties, and how educational institutions prepare students for employment. Advances in generative AI, machine learning, intelligent automation, robotics, and data analytics are enabling machines to undertake an increasing range of cognitive and operational tasks. The Telugu newspaper article “ఏఐ సునామీ… మెల్లిగా ముంచుకొస్తోంది..!!”—approximately translated as “The AI Tsunami Is Slowly Approaching”—provides the thematic foundation for this research paper. The metaphor highlights growing public concern about the speed of technological change and its potential implications for jobs, professional skills, and economic security. However, the relationship between AI and employment is not simply a matter of machines replacing people. AI can automate selected tasks, improve human productivity, create new occupations, and transform existing professions. Its ultimate impact depends on technological capabilities, business decisions, market demand, education systems, and public policy. This paper examines these interconnected issues through a narrative review of relevant research and policy literature, with particular emphasis on India's workforce and digital economy. Research objectives The principal objectives are to: Examine how AI is transforming employment patterns and occupational structures. Distinguish between task automation, occupational transformation, and complete job displacement. Identify sectors and categories of workers that may experience substantial technological disruption. Investigate the emergence of new career opportunities and AI-related professional skills. Analyze the role of education, reskilling, and lifelong learning in workforce adaptation. Explore the implications of AI for income inequality, job security, and socioeconomic inclusion. Develop a conceptual framework for responsible AI adoption and inclusive employment growth in India. Major research themes 1. It considers how automation may reduce demand for certain tasks while changing the responsibilities and skill requirements of existing occupations. 2. Job displacement versus job creation A central theme is the distinction between technological exposure and actual job loss. The paper explores how productivity improvements, business expansion, new products, and emerging occupations may generate employment opportunities, while recognizing that some workers may face displacement or difficult transitions. 3. The changing nature of professional skills The study considers the increasing importance of AI literacy, data interpretation, critical thinking, communication, problem-solving, domain expertise, and responsible technology use. It argues that future employability will depend increasingly on the ability to combine technological tools with human judgment. 4. Economic and social consequences The paper discusses potential effects on wages, job security, career progression, labour-market inequality, and access to economic opportunities. It highlights the possibility that technological benefits may be distributed unevenly unless education, training, and social protection policies address the needs of vulnerable workers. 5. AI and India's employment landscape India presents a particularly important context because of its large workforce, growing digital economy, extensive IT and business-services sectors, manufacturing ambitions, and expanding higher-education system. The paper explores opportunities and risks for graduates, entry-level professionals, technical workers, and small businesses. 6. Education and workforce reskilling The research examines how universities, technical institutions, employers, and vocational training organizations can prepare learners for an AI-enabled economy. It emphasizes practical learning, industry–academia collaboration, continuous professional development, and the importance of developing independent reasoning alongside AI proficiency. 7. Responsible AI and public policy The paper proposes policy directions involving labour-market monitoring, accessible reskilling programmes, worker-transition assistance, responsible workplace deployment, data privacy, human oversight, and inclusive access to technological opportunities. Proposed conceptual contribution The paper introduces a five-pillar conceptual framework for managing AI-driven employment transformation: Technological readiness: Digital infrastructure, reliable data systems, and access to appropriate AI tools. Human capital development: AI literacy, technical education, vocational training, and lifelong learning. Employment transition support: Career guidance, job matching, retraining, and assistance for displaced workers. Responsible AI adoption: Fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency, and appropriate human oversight. Inclusive economic growth: Ensuring that workers, smaller enterprises, and underserved communities can benefit from AI-related opportunities. This framework is a proposed synthesis of the reviewed literature. Its effectiveness would need to be assessed through empirical studies and real-world implementation. Research significance The significance of this research lies in its balanced treatment of AI as both an opportunity for economic development and a potential source of labour-market disruption. Rather than assuming that AI will inevitably eliminate jobs or automatically create sufficient new employment, the paper emphasizes the importance of understanding the conditions under which different outcomes emerge. title: Foundational perspectives on conceptual frameworks for accounting standards: advancing toward a meta-framework
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the conceptual fragmentation within the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) Conceptual Framework (CF) by investigating the interrelationships among three fundamental accounting choices: accounting approaches (balance sheet vs. income statement), capital maintenance concepts (financial vs. physical), and measurement bases (historical cost vs. current value). It aims to develop a comprehensive meta-framework that integrates these elements through broader foundational perspectives. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a normative methodology, the study synthesizes existing theoretical debates and formalizes alternative accounting positions. Through logical analysis, it identifies consistent configurations among the three accounting choices and organizes them into three overarching foundational perspectives: market, entrepreneurial, and institutional. Findings The research demonstrates that coherent links exist among accounting approaches, capital maintenance, and measurement bases. These are structured into three foundational perspectives, each representing a distinct accounting philosophy aligned with different stakeholder needs and epistemological views. The study proposes a meta-framework that integrates these perspectives to enhance conceptual coherence and regulatory flexibility. Research limitations/implications The study is theoretical and lacks empirical validation. Further research is needed to test the applicability of the meta-framework across diverse institutional and cultural contexts and to empirically assess the role of the institutional perspective in CFs. Practical implications The framework helps standard setters, policymakers, and managers tailor accounting practices and regulations to varied stakeholder interests and organizational contexts, improving transparency and relevance in financial reporting. Originality/value The study introduces a novel meta-framework that reinterprets foundational accounting choices through integrated perspectives, offering a more pluralistic and inclusive vision for CFs.

title: Corporate Governance Principles and Sustainable Performance: Exploratory Insights from an Emerging Economy
summary: Purpose: This inquiry was driven by the need to bridge the knowledge gap regarding the relationship between corporate governance principles (CGP) and sustainable performance (SP) in emerging economies (EE). Extant studies have paid limited attention to the interaction between CGP and SP in EE, resulting in limited guidance for policymakers and management teams seeking to promote sustainable corporate practices. Methodology: This study adopted an exploratory qualitative research design based on secondary data. Data were systematically collected from publicly available sources, including annual reports, corporate governance reports, sustainability reports, regulatory submissions, company websites, stock exchange submissions, and relevant industry publications. Relevant regulatory frameworks, corporate governance codes, and telecommunications industry guidelines were also examined. The study explored a Selected Firm (SF) in the telecommunications industry in an emerging economy. For ethical reasons, SF was used to protect the identity of the case study. Findings: Findings reveal that SF demonstrates a strong commitment to corporate governance in several areas but faces concerns regarding limited board independence, inconsistent disclosure of policies, and inadequate mechanisms for addressing emerging risks. These challenges pose risks to the firm’s long-term sustainability and stakeholders’ trust. The findings further indicate that transparency, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), Financial Sustainability (FS), and Service Affordability (SA) are important for sustainable performance in EE. Strengthening board diversity and independence, improving transparency, integrating advanced risk management systems, and fostering open communication with stakeholders can enhance governance effectiveness. The implementation of these principles also requires appropriate theoretical frameworks, including stewardship, agency, and stakeholder theories. Originality: The study contributes to literature by applying an exploratory qualitative approach to examine the relationship between CGP and SP in an emerging economy, an area that remains relatively underexplored.

title: Corporate Governance in Tanzania: Analysing the Implementation of Transparency and Accountability Principles in Private Companies
summary: Background: Transparency and accountability are central to corporate governance, but their implementation in Tanzanian private companies depends on more than the existence of statutory requirements. This article examines the legal and institutional framework governing corporate disclosure, financial reporting, directors' duties, shareholder oversight and beneficial ownership, and considers factors that may constrain implementation. Key Findings: The analysis identifies limited integration of the legal and institutional framework, concentrated ownership and control, limited awareness of governance obligations, weaknesses in monitoring and enforcement, and inadequate internal governance mechanisms as relevant constraints. A conceptual framework drawing on agency and stakeholder perspectives links these constraints to the allocation and exercise of corporate power, the accountability of directors and controlling shareholders, and the protection of shareholders and other legitimate interests. Documentary and institutional evidence, including BRELA compliance and beneficial-ownership activities and relevant judicial decisions, indicates that implementation mechanisms operate within the existing framework. The available evidence does not, however, permit a comprehensive assessment of the prevalence or scale of governance challenges across Tanzania's private-company sector. Conclusion: The article recommends a National Corporate Governance Code for Private Companies establishing mandatory minimum standards, with enhanced requirements proportionate to size, complexity, ownership structure, financing, regulatory status and economic or public-interest significance. Effective implementation should be supported by institutional capacity, risk-based monitoring, beneficial-ownership verification, clearer compliance mechanisms and coordination among relevant institutions.

title: Digital Transformation of Insurance Underwriting in Saudi Arabia: Enhancing Risk Selection, Pricing and Operational Efficiency under Vision 2030
summary: Saudi Arabia’s insurance sector is expanding while simultaneously undergoing regulatory, technological and organizational transformation. Under Vision 2030, digital infrastructure, data and artificial intelligence have become explicit enablers of insurance-sector development, creating a strong policy context for redesigning underwriting. This paper examines how digital transformation can improve risk selection, pricing adequacy and operational efficiency in Saudi insurance underwriting while preserving governance, fairness and professional accountability. An integrative review approach is used to synthesize recent peer-reviewed insurance, artificial-intelligence and financial-technology literature with official Saudi policy and market evidence. The analysis identifies five mutually dependent transformation capabilities: integrated and high-quality data, advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, digitally orchestrated workflows, model governance and explainability, and underwriting talent capable of combining actuarial judgment with digital tools. The paper argues that the greatest value does not arise from replacing underwriters, but from redesigning underwriting as a human-in-the-loop decision system in which routine cases can be automated, complex risks are escalated, and pricing decisions are supported by transparent analytics. Saudi market evidence demonstrates rapid premium growth and an increasingly explicit regulatory focus on technology, data and artificial intelligence. However, implementation risks include fragmented data, algorithmic bias, privacy and cybersecurity concerns, legacy-system integration, model drift and inadequate change management. A Saudi Underwriting Digital Transformation Framework is therefore proposed, linking digital foundations, analytics, workflow redesign, governance safeguards and measurable performance outcomes. The framework provides a research and managerial agenda for insurers seeking to improve technical profitability, customer responsiveness and market resilience while aligning digital underwriting with the objectives of Vision 2030.

title: Treasury and Working Capital Risk Management in Debt-Financed Saudi Enterprises
summary: Saudi enterprises with significant debt obligations encounter a complex treasury challenge: liquidity must sustain daily operations while guaranteeing debt-service capacity amid oscillating interest rates, payment delays, supply disruptions, and evolving refinancing conditions. This integrative review explores the combined governance of treasury and working capital risk management in debt-financed Saudi enterprises, moving beyond the traditional separation of these finance functions. Recent research on working capital, corporate liquidity, debt maturity, hedging, supply-chain finance, and Saudi corporate finance is synthesized using a risk-transmission framework. The findings indicate that cash conversion policy is most effective when managed as a resilience portfolio rather than through simple cycle minimization. Inventory buffers, receivable terms, supplier payments, committed liquidity, debt tenor, interest-rate exposure, covenant headroom, and cash reserves interact in nonlinear ways; enhancing one metric may undermine another if treasury decisions are made in isolation from operations. Saudi-specific evidence further demonstrates that financing constraints and macro-financial conditions influence the reliance on internal cash for investment. Additionally, recent studies highlight the significance of debt maturity, Sharia-compliant capital structures, and precautionary cash holdings. This paper develops an integrated treasury-working-capital risk architecture for Saudi firms, identifies control indicators for boards and treasury committees, and outlines research priorities related to covenant risk, cash-flow-at-risk, supply-chain finance, sukuk-linked liquidity, and sector heterogeneity. The central conclusion is that debt-financed enterprises should prioritize liquidity reliability, rather than solely accounting liquidity, by aligning operating-cycle cash, committed funding, and debt-service obligations within a unified, stress-tested governance framework.
