title: An AI-Driven Machine Learning and Deep Learning Framework for Automated Financial Fraud Detection Using a Forensic Accounting Dashboard
summary: It is becoming increasingly harder to commit financial fraud due to advancements in digital transactions and global financial systems. An innovative system that uses the forensic accounting dashboard for automated discovery and analysis of financial fraud will be developed in this study. This system will use AI, MLA, and data conception approaches to spot any anomaly, suspicious activity, or fraud. The dashboards will provide insights to the forensic accountants by means of predictive analytics and visual representations. The proposed solution will ensure increased accuracy, minimize manual effort and improve efficiency in decision making. This innovation will help enhance fraud preclusion approaches in financial institutions and corporate entities. The objective of this study is to examine the current trends in forensic accounting with respect to financial fraud detection and prevention during this digital era. In this regard, the study analyzes and highlights the current trends in technologies and approaches used in forensic accounting to uncover fraudulent activities, including data analytics, digital forensics, and advanced forensic accounting approaches. In addition, this study analyses rare monitoring systems and their impact on forensic accounting approaches with a special emphasis on corporate governance. This research methodology has allowed a combination of content analysis of case studies of the existing trend in deceptive practices, together with the mediation of forensic accounting. This research is expected to contribute to the encroachment of forensic accounting practices and provide insights for policy makers, practitioners and stakeholders dealing with financial frauds in the current business environment.

title: FROM STRUCTURE TO CAPABILITY: RETHINKING AUDIT COMMITTEE EFFECTIVENESS AND FIRM PERFORMANCE: A NARRATIVE REVIEW
summary: Purpose: This review examines whether, how, and under what conditions audit committee effectiveness, conventionally proxied by independence, financial expertise, size, and diligence, is associated with firm performance, and why prior findings diverge. Design/methodology/approach: A narrative review structured around the SANRA quality criteria synthesises peer-reviewed theoretical, primary empirical, review, and meta-analytic evidence through agency, resource dependence, and institutional theory. Findings: Evidence is strongest for independence and financial expertise, particularly accounting expertise, and is more robust for financial reporting and audit quality outcomes than for firm performance. Meta-analytic evidence links independence, expertise, and committee size to firm performance, whereas meeting frequency shows no significant aggregate association with performance, even though it is linked to lower earnings management. Divergent findings are traced to three sources: reliance on structural proxies that do not capture oversight processes; dynamic endogeneity, whereby prior performance and adverse events reshape committee composition and activity; and institutional variation, including principal-principal conflicts in concentrated-ownership settings. Originality/value: The review develops a process-based framework and five testable propositions linking structural attributes, oversight processes, governance outcomes, and firm outcomes under institutional boundary conditions, and illustrates their relevance using Kenya’s corporate governance code. Research limitations: As a narrative review, the synthesis is interpretive rather than exhaustive, and the proposed mediating pathways remain to be tested empirically. Practical implications: Boards, regulators and investors should assess audit committees on the substance of their oversight, information access, challenge and follow-up-rather than on their formal composition alone. Keywords: audit committee; corporate governance; firm performance; financial expertise; independence; endogeneity; institutional theory; emerging markets; narrative review

title: UTILIZING RESEARCH METHODS IN MODERN FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT AND MARKETING WITHIN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: In the period from 2016 to 2024, the digital economy of Uzbekistan demonstrated rapid growth, increasing its share in gross domestic product (GDP) from 2% to 17%. This growth is driven by the country’s active digital transformation, including widespread adoption of financial technologies (fintech), increased digital marketing penetration, and increased government spending on digital infrastructure and e-governance. As part of the study, an econometric time series analysis was conducted, which revealed an almost perfect correlation between the level of implementation of fintech solutions, the development of digital markets and government digital investments. The results of the least squares regression analysis (OLS) with a coefficient of determination R2 = 0.998 confirm the high significance and explanatory power of the selected factors in the development of the digital economy. The findings indicate that the use of modern econometric and analytical methods significantly improves the accuracy of forecasting financial risks, the effectiveness of marketing investments (ROI), as well as the effectiveness of government economic policy. The recommendations include the introduction of econometric models enhanced by artificial intelligence for small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs), as well as the creation of real-time analytical dashboards. These tools will contribute to inclusive economic growth, the development of innovation and the achievement of the UN Sustainable Development Goal No. 9 (industry, innovation and infrastructure).

title: ЦИФРОВА ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ МІЖНАРОДНОГО МЕНЕДЖМЕНТУ В УМОВАХ РОЗВИТКУ ТЕХНОЛОГІЙ ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ
summary: The rapid advancement of the digital economy and the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence technologies are reshaping the principles and mechanisms of international management. The growing complexity of the global business environment, intensified competition, geopolitical uncertainty, and the continuous expansion of digital data require international companies to transform traditional management approaches and implement intelligent digital solutions capable of supporting strategic and operational decision-making. The purpose of this study is to substantiate the theoretical foundations of the digital transformation of international management by systematizing the application of artificial intelligence technologies across key managerial functions, identifying their managerial effects, and developing a conceptual model that reflects the relationships among external environmental factors, digital technologies, management processes, and organizational performance. The research is based on analysis, synthesis, comparison, systematization, generalization, and structural-logical modeling. The findings demonstrate that artificial intelligence technologies significantly enhance strategic planning, managerial decision-making, human resource management, international marketing, logistics, and financial management by improving analytical capabilities, forecasting accuracy, resource allocation, process automation, and organizational adaptability. A conceptual model of the digital transformation of international management is proposed, integrating external drivers, digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence technologies, managerial functions, organizational mechanisms, and business outcomes into a unified analytical framework. The practical value of the study lies in applying the proposed model to develop digital transformation strategies, improve managerial decision-making, strengthen competitive advantages, and increase the resilience of international companies operating in a rapidly changing global business environment.

title: AI Washing and Stock Returns: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Firms
summary: Artificial intelligence has become increasingly prominent in corporate disclosure, yet firms' AI-related narratives may not always be supported by observable investment in technology or human capital. Using AI-related keywords from annual reports, AI patents, and AI-related job postings of Chinese A-share firms from 2020 to 2025, we construct a firm-year measure to examine this disclosure-investment gap. We classify a firm as an AI washer when its AI-related disclosure is above the industry-year median, while both AI patent activity and AI-related recruitment remain below their corresponding medians. Firms meeting this definition are associated with lower annual stock returns, and the result remains qualitatively unchanged when we use alternative methods to identify AI patents. Additional tests point to two related market responses: AI washing is accompanied by more negative media coverage and weaker investor sentiment. The return discount is also more pronounced among firms with higher institutional ownership and among firms in regions with stronger local AI policy support. These results suggest that investors do not treat AI-related disclosure independently of observable corporate activity. Instead, the impact of AI narratives on stock returns appears to depend partly on whether firms can support those narratives with technological development and hiring.

title: BLOCKCHAIN-ENABLED SUPPLY CHAIN GOVERNANCE FOR MSME MARKET INTEGRATION: A DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION MODEL FOR MODERN RETAIL DISTRIBUTION
summary: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking access to modern retail channels face persistent distribution governance problems arising from fragmented records, limited shipment visibility, and weak product traceability. This study develops a blockchain-enabled digital supply chain governance model and implements it through SerangChain, a web-based prototype designed for MSME-to-retail distribution in Serang, Banten, Indonesia. A Design Science Research approach was employed, covering problem identification, requirement analysis, conceptual model design, prototype development, functional testing, and initial evaluation. The proposed model integrates three layers: supply chain management, a private blockchain-inspired ledger for transparent and verifiable transaction recording, and an analytics layer for monitoring distribution performance. The prototype supports MSME, modern-retail, and administrator roles and includes product management, retail requests, distribution transactions, blockchain ledger records, and analytical dashboards. Functional testing showed that all core modules operated according to the designed workflow, while the ledger simulation generated linked transaction records containing transaction IDs, block IDs, timestamps, previous hashes, and verification status. The findings indicate that a lightweight blockchain-inspired architecture can strengthen information transparency, traceability, and digital accountability without requiring a complex public blockchain infrastructure. Because field-based User Acceptance Testing and full impact measurement are still ongoing, claims regarding efficiency improvement remain preliminary. The study contributes a governance-oriented digital transformation model that can support MSME market integration with modern retail and provides a practical foundation for subsequent empirical validation.

title: Privacy in India’s digital credit ecosystem: a systematic literature review and policy directions
summary: This study examines India’s digital credit ecosystem, exploring the relationship between technological efficiency and user rights, particularly data privacy. It aims to identify emerging trends, key concerns, and potential regulatory and technological interventions. The PRISMA framework guided a systematic review of scholarly literature on digital credit services, data privacy, and global benchmarks. A filtered collection of 198 documents formed the final corpus for analysis. Through bibliometric analysis (inductive approach), we identified dominant research themes, while content analysis (deductive approach) classified the literature by keyword frequency related to data collection, storage, and breach impacts. The study highlights three key research themes: (1) India’s rapidly expanding digital credit ecosystem, (2) emerging financial data privacy developments, and (3) international approaches to privacy in financial services. India’s digital lending is experiencing exponential growth, driven by FinTech innovations and data integration. However, concerns persist regarding data accuracy, transparency, and privacy. Emerging technologies such as Blockchain and Federated Learning offer promising solutions to mitigate privacy risks and enhance compliance. The findings provide context-specific directions for strengthening privacy governance within India’s digital credit ecosystem. Specifically, they offer practical guidance for regulators, policymakers, financial institutions, and FinTech firms seeking to promote responsible digital lending and sustainable financial inclusion.

title: Corporate Fraud and Corporate Accountability in India: A Critical Study of the Companies Act, 2013
summary: Corporate fraud has emerged as one of the most serious challenges to corporate governance and investor confidence in India. The growth of the corporate sector, the increasing complexity of financial transactions, the separation of ownership and management, and the extensive delegation of managerial powers have created opportunities for corporate misconduct. Corporate fraud may take several forms, including manipulation of financial statements, misappropriation of company assets, fraudulent related-party transactions, falsification of accounts, concealment of material information and abuse of managerial position. Such activities adversely affect shareholders, creditors, employees, investors and the economy as a whole. The Companies Act, 2013 represents an important legislative attempt to strengthen corporate accountability and prevent fraudulent corporate practices in India. Section 447 specifically provides for punishment for fraud, while Sections 211 and 212 establish the statutory framework for the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) and the investigation of serious corporate fraud. The Act further strengthens accountability through provisions relating to directors’ duties, auditor responsibilities, internal controls, audit committees, vigil mechanisms, related-party transactions, investigation and class-action remedies. The statutory framework therefore adopts both preventive and punitive approaches towards corporate misconduct. This paper critically analyses the concept of corporate fraud and the mechanisms of corporate accountability under the Companies Act, 2013. It examines the role of directors, auditors, independent directors, audit committees, the SFIO and other regulatory mechanisms in preventing and investigating corporate fraud. The study finds that the Companies Act, 2013 has significantly strengthened India’s corporate fraud regime, but challenges remain in relation to enforcement delays, complex corporate structures, auditor independence, inter-agency coordination, whistle-blower protection and technological forms of fraud. The paper recommends stronger preventive governance, improved forensic investigation, enhanced accountability of corporate gatekeepers and more effective regulatory coordination.

title: The interplay between renewable energy, green finance, and economic development: A bibliometric review
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractResearch on the relationships among green finance, renewable energy, and economic development has expanded rapidly in recent years; however, the intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, and thematic evolution of this interdisciplinary field remain insufficiently understood. This study addresses this gap by conducting a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny, the web interface of the bibliometrix R package. The analytical framework integrates performance analysis with science mapping techniques, including keyword co-occurrence, citation, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, thematic mapping, and thematic evolution analyses. The findings reveal substantial growth in scientific production and increasing international collaboration, while identifying an intellectual foundation primarily shaped by studies on econometric methodologies, the relationships between economic growth and environmental sustainability, and the integration of green finance with energy economics. Four major research streams emerge: green financial instruments and markets; the finance, growth, and emissions nexus; renewable energy transition and policy; and advanced quantitative modeling approaches. Thematic evolution further indicates that, although green finance, renewable energy, and sustainable development remain the core research themes, emerging topics such as digital finance and the digital economy are receiving increasing scholarly attention. By providing a comprehensive knowledge map of the field, this study contributes to a better understanding of its intellectual foundations, conceptual development, and future research directions, while offering valuable insights for researchers and policymakers seeking to promote sustainable finance, renewable energy transition, and long-term economic development.

title: Audit of the effectiveness of SME support in the context of the digital transformation of human resources of the supreme audit institution
summary: This article aims to analyze the practical application of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies as a transformative factor for the human resource potential of the Supreme Audit Institution (SAI). The study focuses on the audit of the effectiveness of state support within the small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) sector of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The integration of AI algorithms into SAI activities fundamentally redefines the role of the state auditor, transforming them into a data analyst capable of identifying latent correlations between state support volumes and the qualitative growth of the enterprise sector. The study reveals a critical discrepancy: while there is a formal increase in the number of SMEs, current financial incentives in low-tech sectors remain largely ineffective. The findings suggest that the traditional audit system, lacking advanced data analytics, merely records budget absorption indicators without evaluating their impact on the technological complexity and productivity of the businesses involved. The originality of this research lies in the conceptualization of a fundamentally new model of state audit, in which AI serves as the primary driver of transforming SAI human capital. The practical significance is underscored by the development of algorithmic tools for "smart" monitoring of state support, integrated with national databases. The study justifies a methodology for detecting hidden inefficiency risks by automatically benchmarking allocated funds against SMEs' actual contribution to the country’s economic development.

title: Global Supply Chain Shocks and Inflation in a Diversifying Oil Economy: Sustainability Implications for Saudi Arabia
summary: This study examines the effects of global supply chain shocks on inflation in Saudi Arabia, using monthly data from January 2014 to March 2026. Supply chain resilience has emerged as a critical dimension of economic sustainability, yet its inflationary consequences in commodity-dependent economies remain insufficiently understood. The analysis applies both Structural Vector Autoregression (SVAR) and Local Projection (LP) models to estimate impulse response functions. Inflation is measured using the wholesale price index (WPI) and its primary components. Findings from both methodologies are consistent, demonstrating that global supply chain shocks have positive, statistically significant impacts on most measures of wholesale price inflation in the short to medium term. The magnitude and persistence of these effects differ across components. In proportional terms, the most pronounced responses are found in ores and minerals and agricultural products—sectors closely tied to food security and sustainable resource management. However, their contribution to the aggregate WPI depends on their relative weights, with higher-weight categories, particularly metal products, machinery and equipment and food-related products, contributing more to aggregate wholesale price movements. Although the effects diminish in statistical significance over longer horizons, the cumulative responses indicate that supply chain disruptions can leave a persistent upward effect on wholesale price levels across specific categories, even after the direct inflationary impulse has subsided. These findings underscore the importance of building supply chain resilience as part of broader strategies for sustainable economic stability, with direct implications for monetary policy and inflation management in resource-dependent economies.

title: When Growth Destroys Collateral: Technological Obsolescence and Macroprudential Risk in the AI Era
summary: Abstract Schumpeterian growth creates by destroying. A critical financial consequence arises when capital rendered obsolete by innovation also serves as collateral for debt that markets treat as safe. Using the AI infrastructure boom as a case study, this paper documents the scale of investment, the spread of asset-backed and structured finance, and the emergence of investment-grade claims backed by data centres, GPUs, leases, and customer contracts that are increasingly reaching the portfolios of institutional investors. Systemic risk arises not from technological depreciation itself, but from a common collateral revaluation that transforms widely held, information-insensitive claims into information-sensitive ones. Such a shift can trigger screening, abrupt repricing, deleveraging, and fire sales across institutional portfolios. The mechanism echoes a central lesson of the Global Financial Crisis and carries implications for financial supervision, risk assessment, and complementary industrial policy.

title: The paradigm of maritime sustainability and the evolution of the MARPOL regulatory framework
summary: Maritime transport is essential to global trade but generates significant environmental pressures through operational discharges, atmospheric emissions, ballast-water transfers and accidental pollution. This paper examines the environmental footprint of shipping, the structure and function of the MARPOL regulatory framework, Romania’s role in implementing international requirements, and the challenges associated with the transition toward sustainable maritime transport. The discussion is organized around the current research context, the regulatory framework, the analytical approach and the implications for future environmental governance. Particular attention is given to the relationship between environmental protection, technological innovation, regulatory enforcement and the economic continuity of maritime trade.

title: GREEN TECH PARADOX An Analysis of AI in Environment Sustainability
summary: Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into environmental sustainability strategies presents a critical dilemma known as the "Green Tech Paradox." While AI offers unprecedented capabilities to optimize resource allocation, predict climate patterns, and enhance energy efficiency across industrial sectors, its deployment carries substantial, often overlooked, ecological costs. This research provides a critical analysis of the dual role AI plays as both a catalyst for eco-innovations and a significant contributor to environmental degradation. On the positive frontier, AI-driven applications accelerate sustainability by enabling smart power grids, improving carbon capture systems, facilitating precision agriculture, and modeling complex environmental crises. Machine learning algorithms enhance operational efficiency, reducing waste and carbon footprints in manufacturing and logistics. However, these beneficial outcomes are counterbalanced by the escalating physical footprint of AI infrastructure. The training and continuous execution of complex neural networks demand massive amounts of electricity, heavily relying on fossil-fuel-dominant energy grids. Furthermore, data centers consume millions of liters of freshwater daily for cooling mechanisms, accelerating localized water scarcity, while the rapid obsolescence of specialized hardware generates growing volumes of hazardous electronic waste. This paper evaluates this structural tension through a multidimensional synthesis of secondary data, life-cycle assessments, and resource consumption metrics across global data centers. The analysis reveals that without stringent regulatory frameworks and sustainable design interventions, the environmental degradation caused by AI's hardware lifecycle risks surpassing its ecological benefits. Ultimately, the study advocates for a paradigm shift toward "Green AI"—prioritizing algorithmic efficiency, renewable energy integration for computing infrastructure, sustainable hardware lifecycle management, and policy-driven eco-design standards. By establishing transparent auditing protocols, researchers and industry leaders can mitigate the hidden ecological liabilities of artificial intelligence, ensuring that modern technological advancement aligns genuinely with global net-zero targets and long-term planetary boundaries. Keywords: Green AI, Climate change mitigation, Sustainable development goals (SDGs), Environmental governance, Lifecycle assessment of AI.

title: THE IMPORTANCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN IMPROVING ACCOUNTING IN THE CONTEXT OF THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: This study examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in transforming the accounting system amid the rapid development of the digital economy. The research uses content analysis of the scientific literature, a comparative analysis of traditional and digital accounting, a synthesis of secondary statistical data from international consulting firms, and a descriptive analysis of Uzbekistan’s digital tax platforms. The results show that machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, predictive analytics and anomaly detection do more than automate accounting tasks: they speed up financial data processing, reduce human error and support strategic management decisions. The discussion addresses the changing role of the accountant and the opportunities specific to Uzbekistan. The conclusion sets out promising directions for the transition from traditional accounting to “intelligent systems” and offers practical recommendations.

title: Practical Reflections on ESG Construction and CEO Accountability Mechanisms of Enterprises in Emerging Markets under the Framework of Corporate Governance
summary: The rapid growth of the ESG concept in developing nations is an indicator of the global flow of cash for good and a reminder of the inadaptability of institutional transplanting. This article considers the accountability mechanism of senior executives within the framework of the governance environment of developing markets and the construction of ESG. Morningstar research shows the global sustainable fund assets will hit $3.7 trillion by 2025. Some 56 governments have signed up to the ISSB principles. But study by the MIT Sloan School of Management shows that the ESG ratings of six leading agencies have relatively low consistency for companies in emerging nations. Structural restrictions, such weak rules and poor quality data, can also impede emerging economies. In domestic practice, the 2024 "Guidelines for Listed Companies on Sustainable Development Reporting" released by the CSRC pays greater attention to the procedural compliance requirements, and does not place sufficient restrictions on the substantive decision-making responsibilities of senior executives. The Ministry of Finance issued the 2024 "Corporate Sustainable Disclosure Standards—Basic Guidelines (Trial)" that gives a blueprint for the system using global experience and Chinese characteristics. This study considers that it is crucial to develop a governance loop that aligns "capability, responsibility and incentive" to get out of the situation.

title: Dual-Policy Coverage and Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence from China’s Commercial Logistics Node City Program and Supply Chain Innovation and Application Pilot Program
summary: Logistics network development and supply chain organizational innovation may create external conditions for corporate green innovation. Using 30,700 firm-year observations for Chinese A-share listed companies from 2012 to 2024, this study examines the relationship between joint coverage by the Commercial Logistics Node City Program and the Supply Chain Innovation and Application Pilot Program and corporate green innovation. Double machine learning is employed to account flexibly for nonlinear relationships between policy coverage, firm characteristics, and green innovation. Dual-policy coverage is positively and significantly associated with green invention patent applications, with a baseline coefficient of 0.1131. The result remains positive under alternative cross-fitting folds, machine learning algorithms, sample restrictions, and measures of green innovation. Channel analyses indicate that dual-policy coverage is associated with greater supply chain digitalization, lower supply chain risk, and higher innovation efficiency. The estimated association is stronger among firms with higher R&D intensity and weaker among firms facing greater environmental uncertainty. These findings provide firm-level evidence that logistics connectivity and supply chain organizational conditions are relevant to corporate green innovation and offer policy implications for sustainable industrial development.

title: The Triadic Law of Infrastructure Resilience: De-Risking Capital Allocation via the Three-Point Architecture Principle
summary: Large-scale infrastructure investments routinely suffer from severe stranded asset risk and mispriced capital due to fragmented, highly customized, project-by-project engineering designs. To address this structural vulnerability, this paper introduces a novel infrastructure risk-assessment framework grounded in Charles Sanders Peirce’s metaphysical theory of "Thirdness" and the cybernetic Input-Process-Output (IPO) model, proving that an infrastructure asset’s long-term resilience depends entirely on the structural protection of its Intermediate element. By operationalizing the Three-Point Architecture Principle (End 1 → Intermediate → End 2), we demonstrate that a true, stable system only exists when two terminal nodes are mediated by an independent structural interface. We establish that while the endpoints represent highly variable, modular technologies, the Intermediate element represents the capital-intensive core that dictates overall systemic longevity. From this triadic law, we derive a practical Dual-Question Screening Protocol for institutional investors, requiring assets to satisfy a rigorous Segregation Test and a Lifecycle Continuity Mandate before capital allocation. Finally, we demonstrate how critical secondary underwriting risks—including counterparty insolvency, technological obsolescence, regulatory spillover, and CapEx volatility—can be directly diagnosed and neutralized by evaluating the boundary rules of the intermediate interface. Ultimately, this framework shifts infrastructure due diligence from chaotic, project-level engineering reviews to a systematic, boundary-enforced protocol that unlocks embedded real options and compresses equity risk premiums for long-term institutional capital.

title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT PROCESSES IN THE ECONOMIES OF UZBEKISTAN AND AZERBAIJAN
summary: This article presents a comparative analysis of business development processes and the formation of the entrepreneurial environment in the economies of Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan. The study examines mechanisms for supporting small businesses and private entrepreneurship, investment climate, tax policy, digital economy, export potential, and the impact of economic reforms on business development in both countries. In addition, the role of business activity in economic growth, employment, and regional development is evaluated based on statistical indicators. As a result of the research, scientific and practical recommendations aimed at improving the business environment were developed based on the experiences of Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan.

title: Sleepless governments under the land dilemma: farmland pressure and overtime work of local governments
summary: Farmland pressure is a central issue in farmland protection and food security, yet its administrative cost to local governments, as reflected in the intensity of government overtime work, remains largely unmeasured. Matching daily night-time light data with the spatial coordinates of local government headquarters, this paper investigates the impact of farmland pressure on government overtime intensity across 300 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2012 to 2023. Using traditional and Bartik instrumental variables and Double Machine Learning (DML) estimations, we find that rising farmland pressure significantly intensifies government overtime, robust to a series of checks. The effect is muted in large cities and regions with rich cultural endowments or lower fiscal self-sufficiency. Mechanism tests show that farmland pressure drives bureaucratic overwork through increased public service provision, intensified environmental governance mandates, and expanded land allocation quotas. We conclude with policy implications for appraisal reform, governance tools, and civil servants’ well-being.

title: Optimal Control Strategies for Financial Literacy and Loan Repayment Dynamics among MSMEs in Kenya
summary: Financial instability and weak loan repayment performance remain major constraints on the growth and sus tainability of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Kenya. Low levels of financial literacy and digital-finance integration, inflexible debt conditions, inadequate buffers to liquidity and operational stress reduce the stability of cash flows and increase vulnerability to default. In this study, a five-control optimal control model is developed for financial interventions to enhance the financial literacy and loan repayment dynamics of MSMEs. A system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations represents the interactions among financial literacy, financial health, loan burden, cash reserves, and operational stress. Bounded controls are financial literacy training, FinTech support, loan restructuring flexibility, emergency liquidity injection and business mentorship. The application of Pontryagin’s maximum principle leads to the derivation of the Hamiltonian, adjoint equations, transversality conditions, and optimal control characterisations. The resulting optimality system is solved numerically using a forward–backward sweep method with a fourth- order Runge-Kutta scheme. The simulations indicate that FinTech support has the most significant individual impact as it directly boosts the capacity of repayments, while literacy training and mentorship improve financial decisions and lessen stress-related pressures. Loan restructuring and liquidity injection offer further support on the back of an integrated approach. Some of the benefits of the five-control package can be obtained in the reduced three-control package (u1, u2, u5), which results in a very similar financial health trajectory, and in debt reduction, which is slightly faster in the five-control package. The results show that structured financial education, digital repayment mechanisms, flexible restructuring, liquidity support, and mentorship can result in better repayment outcomes and boost MSME resilience. The model provides a quantitative framework for governments, financial institutions, and development agencies to design timely and cost-conscious enterprise support policies in developing economies.

title: SPECIFIC FEATURES OF IMPROVING ACCOUNTING AND AUDITING SERVICES BASED ON INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS (THE EXPERIENCE OF UZBEKISTAN)
summary: This article analyzes the theoretical and practical aspects of improving accounting and auditing services based on international standards. In particular, it highlights the importance of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and International Standards on Auditing (ISA) in economic development. It also examines the processes of adapting accounting and auditing activities to international standards in the Republic of Uzbekistan, the normative-legal documents adopted in this direction, and the ongoing reforms. The article analyzes the issues of training specialists with international accounting certificates in the country, increasing the transparency of financial reporting, and creating a favorable investment climate for investors. Furthermore, it outlines the problems arising during the implementation of international standards and ways to overcome them. The research results can serve to strengthen the integration of the country's economy into the international financial system by improving accounting and auditing services.

title: Stock Market Development, Economic Growth and Environmental Sustainability in South Africa: A Cointegration and Time–Frequency Analysis
summary: The development of stock markets can influence both economic growth and environmental sustainability, yet whether financial market expansion can achieve these objectives simultaneously remains unclear in emerging economies. This study examines the effects of stock market development (SMD) on economic growth and carbon emissions in South Africa over 1975–2022 using autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) models and wavelet coherence analysis. The ARDL estimates reveal predominantly negative or insignificant effects on economic growth, while nonlinear specifications indicate that positive growth effects emerge at higher levels of market development. Similarly, market capitalization and trading activity increasingly exhibit positive associations with carbon emissions after 1994, suggesting that financial deepening can reinforce emission-intensive economic activity. In contrast, greater market breadth is associated with lower emissions. Wavelet coherence further demonstrates substantial time- and frequency-dependent relationships, with post-1994 financial integration marking stronger stock market–growth and stock market–emission linkages. Short-run emission reductions during major crises appear temporary, reflecting contractions in economic and market activity. These findings suggest that stock market expansion alone cannot deliver sustainable growth. Policy should therefore ‘green’ financial development by directing capital toward renewable energy, clean technologies, and low-carbon firms while strengthening ESG disclosure, environmental compliance, and climate-related financial regulation.

title: Beyond digitalization: how entrepreneurial orientation and competitive advantage drive tourism MSME performance
summary: Purpose: to examine the effects of digital transformation and entrepreneurial orientation on tourism MSME performance in Semarang City, Indonesia, with competitive advantage serving as a mediating variable. Method: this study employed a quantitative explanatory approach using a cross-sectional survey of 200 tourism MSME owners or managers in Semarang City, Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and analysed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 to evaluate the measurement model and test the proposed hypotheses. Findings: digital transformation and entrepreneurial orientation positively influence tourism MSME performance and competitive advantage. Competitive advantage also positively affects business performance and partially mediates the relationships between digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, and MSME performance. These findings highlight the importance of integrating digital capabilities and entrepreneurial strategies to strengthen competitive advantage and improve tourism MSME performance. Implications: integrating digital capabilities and entrepreneurial strategies can strengthen competitive advantage and improve tourism MSME performance. Originality: lies in integrating digital transformation and entrepreneurial orientation to explain tourism MSME performance, with competitive advantage serving as a mediating mechanism.

title: Rural household waste sorting and its social, environmental and economic impacts: implications for sustainable governance
summary: Purpose This study addresses the “last-mile” governance dilemma of rural household waste sorting in developing countries, where participation is high but effectiveness is low. Guided by public-goods, externality, and collective-action theories, it aims to investigate two main questions: (1) what are the multidimensional (environmental, health, economic and social) welfare effects of rural waste sorting and (2) how do these effects vary across public and private domains, challenging the assumption that the benefits of waste sorting are homogeneous. Design/methodology/approach The study utilizes survey data collected from 939 rural households across two distinct regions in China: Jiangsu and Gansu. To rigorous analyze the data while accounting for potential self-selection bias and unobserved heterogeneity among participants, the authors employ a sophisticated econometric approach. Specifically, they combine Propensity Score Matching (PSM) with an endogenous switching regression (ESR) model. This methodology ensures robust causal inference regarding the multidimensional welfare effects and allows for a detailed comparison of outcomes between public and private behavioral domains. Findings Waste sorting yields positive but uneven welfare effects, following a gradient of social > environmental > health > economic benefits. This indicates that current participation is primarily driven by social norms rather than economic or health returns. Crucially, situational context matters: informal normative pressure in the public domain inflates perceived environmental benefits. Robustness checks reveal a “numerical illusion,” showing that the environmental effects realized through externally mobilized participation may be overestimated by up to 25.4%, highlighting a gap between reported and actual governance success. Originality/value This study advances behavioral and environmental governance research by dismantling the assumption of homogeneous welfare effects in waste sorting. Academically, it is among the first to quantify domain-specific, multidimensional outcomes and expose a significant measurement bias (“numerical illusion”) in public interventions. For policymakers and managers, it provides a crucial diagnostic framework to shift rural governance from arbitrary, campaign-driven participation targets toward outcome-based, scenario-adapted incentives that tie behavioral outcomes to tangible economic and health returns.

title: РОЗВИТОК СУЧАСНИХ СИСТЕМ БЕЗГОТІВКОВИХ РОЗРАХУНКІВ В УКРАЇНІ: ІНСТИТУЦІЙНІ ТА ПОВЕДІНКОВІ ДЕТЕРМІНАНТИ ФОРМУВАННЯ ДОВІРИ
summary: This article examines the fundamental transformation of the modern cashless payment system and identifies the determinants of trust among economic actors as a key factor in the acceptance and use of such systems in real life. The aim of the study is to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the institutional, technological, systemic, and behavioral factors influencing the formation of trust among economic agents in modern cashless payment systems amid digitalization and regulatory transformations in Ukraine. A systematic review has been carried out of current technological trends in the operation of cashless payment systems (in-app payments, SoftPOS, AI agents, Open Banking), and the barriers to their adoption and associated risks (loss of privacy, cyber-attacks, the ‘invisible money’ effect) that are hindering the further development of cashless payments have been identified. Users’ preference for cashless payments results from a trade-off between their subjective perception of potential benefits and the challenges associated with their reluctance to accept the drawbacks. The concept of economic agents’ trust in the non-cash payment system is structured, and its components—institutional, agent-based, systemic, technological and informal—are described. A retrospective analysis has been carried out of the trends in the share of non-cash transactions in Ukraine and the level of trust/distrust in the banking sector over the last two decades. It has been argued that the technical readiness of the infrastructure merely creates the potential for the further development of cashless payments, whilst it is the level of trust that determines the actual scale of operation of cashless payment systems. The paper highlights the need to develop strategies to enhance all components of trust, harmonise the concept of Open Banking, and minimise the cognitive burden on economic agents, taking behavioural factors into account. It notes that the rapid growth in the proportion of cashless transactions in Ukraine confirms the Ukrainian population’s flexibility and adaptability to innovations in the field of cashless payments. It has been noted that the restoration and growth of confidence in the National Bank of Ukraine and banking institutions is creating a synergistic effect for the further development of modern fintech services and the digitalisation of the economy.

title: AIVO Brand Alpha Index: US Small-Business Banking
summary: The AIVO Brand Alpha Index measures how often AI assistants recommend a brand compared with its share of the market, and estimates what the gap is worth. This first edition covers US small-business banking. It draws on 1,080 four-turn conversations on ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, run on 18 September 2026, in which the business owner never named a bank. The conversations cover four situations: starting a business, switching banks, seeking credit and banking internationally. Eighteen major banks are scored from 0 to 100, where 50 indicates recommendation in line with market share. Fintech and non-bank providers received 77% of recommendations. Sixteen of the 18 banks fall below parity, twelve are rated Severe and five were not recommended in any conversation. Annual revenue impact is estimated per $100m of new small-business banking revenue. The method follows AIVO Brand Alpha v2.0. This report is DOI-anchored and has not been peer reviewed.

title: LEGAL CONFLICTS IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: THE UKRAINIAN AND EUROPEAN EXPERIENCE
summary: This article examines the ethical and legal issues arising in the digital economy. These conflicts are conceptualised as contradictions between innovative technological practices, ethical norms and applicable legislation. Three key types of conflict are identified: those relating to privacy and data monetisation, algorithmic autonomy and accountability, and digital security and fundamental rights. Particular emphasis is placed on the wartime context in Ukraine, which presents unique challenges for digital transformation and legal regulation. Methodology. The research methodology employed is a synthesis of the comparative legal method and a Law and Economics approach. The comparative legal method is employed to compare the regulatory instruments of the European Union (GDPR, AI Act, DSA, DMA) with those of Ukraine (the Laws of Ukraine ‘On Personal Data Protection’, ‘On Virtual Assets’, ‘On Media’, and ‘On Electronic Communications’). The empirical basis of the study comprises reports by the European Commission (Digital Economy and Society Index, DESI), Eurostat statistical data on the digital transformation of EU Member States, and analytical materials published by the OECD (Digital Economy Outlook) and the World Bank (Digital Development Report). The Law and Economics analysis is employed to evaluate the impact of legal conflicts on the investment climate, transaction costs and innovation activity. Results. The study demonstrates that the development of the digital economy in Ukraine and the European Union is determined not only by the pace of digital technology adoption, but also by the quality of the institutional environment in which digital markets operate. The European model is distinguished by the establishment of common rules governing data flows, the utilisation of artificial intelligence, and the operation of digital platforms. This contributes to a reduction in regulatory uncertainty for businesses and the creation of conditions conducive to long-term investment in digital technologies. Ukraine continues to face an institutional and technological gap with the EU, as evidenced by uneven levels of business digitalisation, limited investment capacity among some businesses in digital infrastructure, and heightened risks associated with the use of data and artificial intelligence technologies. At the same time, a lack of clear rules governing the digital economy could lead to higher transaction costs for businesses, reduce investment activity and make it more difficult for Ukrainian companies to access the European digital market. The study establishes that digital regulatory conflicts have not only legal but also direct economic effects: they affect regulatory compliance costs, the level of market competition, access to digital services, consumer trust, and the ability of businesses to scale digital business models. In this context, the harmonisation of Ukraine's digital environment with European approaches may be regarded as one of the factors reducing institutional barriers to digital investment and deepening Ukraine's economic integration with the EU. Practical Implications. The practical value of the findings lies in their potential application to shaping Ukraine's economic policy on digital transformation, aimed not merely at regulatory adaptation but, above all, at creating conditions to increase enterprise productivity, attract investment, and expand the participation of Ukrainian firms in European digital markets. Priority areas include reducing regulatory and transaction costs for digital businesses; establishing rules for data flows and AI deployment that align with the European market; promoting the digitalisation of small and medium-sized enterprises; developing digital infrastructure; and encouraging competition in digital markets. The implementation of these measures takes on additional economic significance under martial law, as digital technologies can ensure business continuity, reduce the costs of coordinating economic processes and boost enterprise resilience to external shocks. Therefore, the effectiveness of harmonisation with European digital regulations should be assessed not only by the number of provisions implemented, but also by their impact on investment activity, productivity, competitiveness and the resilience of Ukraine’s digital economy. Value / Originality. The scientific novelty of the study lies in its identification of the economic consequences of regulatory and ethico-legal conflicts arising during the digital transformation of Ukraine's economy and its integration into the European digital space. The proposed typology of key conflicts enables the systematisation of factors that generate regulatory uncertainty, increase transaction costs, and affect investment activity and the competitiveness of digital economy enterprises. The developed cyclical model of conflict evolution is intended as a tool for identifying the interrelationship between technological change, regulatory adaptation, economic costs, and institutional responses. Its application may prove useful in assessing the digital resilience of the economy, underpinning public policy on digital transformation, and setting priorities for Ukraine's economic integration into the European digital market amid wartime conditions and post-conflict recovery.

title: State Policy and Strategic Planning for Sectoral Digital Development
summary: Abstract This article explores the crucial role of state policy in driving digital development. It analyzes the factors influencing digital policies at international, national, and regional levels. The study proposes specific indicators and tools to assess the effectiveness of digital development policies at national or regional levels, as well as within specific sectors. A pilot implementation of this assessment is conducted in several priority sectors of the Russian Federation. The article concludes with recommendations for improving state policies related to sectoral digital transformation.

title: A Hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Framework for Prioritizing Supply Chain Risks in Perishable Food Manufacturing
summary: Abstract Food-processing supply chains are severely threatened by interruptions in procurement, storage and transport due to the perishability of products and the strict delivery demands. Conventional risk models rank the importance of the factors, but do not differentiate the root causes from the downstream consequences. The study proposes a multi-method framework for assessing ten critical disruption factors with the use of expert judgments. AHP Establishes priority weights for strategic intervention. (F6) was perceived as the most important (RII) = 0.9857, but (F10) was the key root-cause driver (D - R = 1.574). AHP validated F10 as the highest priority for intervention (weight: 0.2189), followed by storage violations (F7) and demand spikes (F8). Highly visible disruptions are often symptoms not root causes. title: Internal Control Systems and Financial Reporting Quality: The Moderating Role of Firm Leverage in Non-Financial Firms Listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange
summary: This study examined whether firm leverage moderates the association between internal control systems and financial reporting quality among non-financial firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). Financial reporting quality is essential to investor confidence and effective capital-market oversight, yet internal control systems may not deliver uniform outcomes across firms facing different financial pressures. The study used a positivist philosophy, a deductive approach and an explanatory longitudinal panel design. Secondary data were drawn from annual reports, audited financial statements and corporate-governance disclosures for 26 firms selected from a population of 39 non-financial listed firms that met the stated continuous-listing and data-availability criteria, covering 2010–2025 (416 firm-year observations). Internal controls were operationalised through an Internal Control Disclosure Index (ICDI) based on the five COSO components; leverage was measured as total liabilities divided by total assets; and financial reporting quality was proxied by the inverse of discretionary accruals estimated using the modified Jones model. Fixed-effects panel regression with firm-clustered robust standard errors showed a positive association between the ICDI and reporting quality (β = 1.497, p < .001) and a positive direct association between leverage and reporting quality (β = 0.566, p < .001). The interaction term was negative and statistically significant (β = −1.767, p < .001), indicating that the positive association between disclosed internal controls and reporting quality weakened as leverage increased. The study recommends that regulators, boards and lenders should assess internal-control disclosures alongside leverage exposure. This study provides evidence on how internal controls affect financial reporting quality, accountability, and the reliability of financial information.

title: Oil and Gas Operations and Environmental Security in EGI Communities, Rivers State: An Assessment of Total energies' Operations, 2010-2025
summary: This study examined the types and ways in which TotalEnergies conducts oil and gas operations in Egi communities, Rivers State, Nigeria, and assessed stakeholder perceptions of the environmental-security aspects of pollution associated with these operations between 2010 and 2025. Oil and gas activity in Obite, Obagi and Egita, communities of Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni Local Government Area, has spanned exploration, drilling, gas processing and pipeline transportation for more than five decades, yet the environmental and security consequences of this activity for host communities remain inadequately documented in the scholarly literature. The study was anchored on Environmental Security Theory and the Environmental Justice Framework, which jointly illuminate how ecological degradation threatens human and community security and how the resulting burdens fall inequitably on communities with limited power to resist them. A qualitative case study design was adopted, guided by an interpretivist paradigm. Data were generated through six focus group discussions involving thirty-six participants and twelve in-depth interviews, for a total of forty-eight respondents purposively drawn from traditional rulers and chiefs, Community Development Committee representatives, youth and women representatives, farmers and fishermen across the three communities, and analysed thematically using the six-step framework of Braun and Clarke. Findings showed that TotalEnergies' operations, comprising ageing pipelines, gas flaring, flow stations and periodic well and pipeline failures, including the 2012 Egita gas eruption, have produced sustained air, land and water pollution, while stakeholders overwhelmingly perceive these environmental changes as a direct threat to their food, water, health and community security, with decliningagricultural and fishing livelihoods increasingly linked to youth restiveness, oil theft and rising community insecurity. The study recommends improved pipeline integrity management, independent environmental monitoring, restoration of degraded farmland and fishing grounds, and structured community engagement in environmental governance.

title: Epistemologi Indigenous: Kearifan Lokal sebagai Sumber Pengetahuan Alternatif dalam Filsafat Ilmu, Keadilan Epistemik, dan Pembangunan Berkelanjutan
summary: This article examines Indigenous epistemology, its role in critiquing epistemic dominance, and its relevance to environmental law and sustainable development. It focuses on how the recognition of Indigenous peoples can extend beyond the acknowledgment of their identities and collective rights to include recognition of their epistemic authority in environmental decision-making. This study employs normative juridical research using statutory and conceptual approaches, complemented by functional comparison based on practices documented in the literature. The research materials comprise national legislation, international instruments, and scholarly literature on Indigenous knowledge, epistemic justice, and environmental governance. The analysis yields three main findings. First, Indigenous epistemology constitutes a knowledge system that integrates ecological experience, communal validation, ethical-spiritual orientations, and intergenerational transmission, with characteristics that vary across community contexts. Second, its critique of epistemic dominance targets hierarchical mechanisms that marginalize Indigenous knowledge holders without dismissing the importance of scientific scrutiny and dialogue across knowledge systems. Third, epistemic recognition in environmental law requires meaningful participation, the protection of Indigenous knowledge, context-sensitive evidentiary assessment, and accountability mechanisms in decision-making. Based on these findings, this article proposes the Recognition Model, comprising six dimensions: ontological relationality, ecological knowledge, communal validation, ethical-spiritual orientation, intergenerational transmission, and norms and institutionalization. A literature-based examination of Subak, Sasi, and Ammatoa Kajang practices explores the model’s conceptual applicability in Indonesia. The article’s novelty lies in integrating epistemic dimensions into an analytical framework for environmental law institutions. The Recognition Model is proposed as an initial conceptual framework that requires empirical validation in collaboration with Indigenous communities. Its implementation should account for internal community diversity, the rights of knowledge holders, and ecological carrying capacity to promote more inclusive and equitable environmental governance. Abstrak Artikel ini mengkaji epistemologi indigenous, posisinya dalam kritik terhadap dominasi pengetahuan, serta relevansinya bagi hukum lingkungan dan pembangunan berkelanjutan. Fokus kajian terletak pada bagaimana pengakuan terhadap masyarakat adat dapat diperluas dari pengakuan identitas dan hak kolektif menuju pengakuan atas otoritas epistemik mereka dalam pengambilan keputusan lingkungan. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan dan konseptual, serta perbandingan fungsional berdasarkan praktik yang terdokumentasi dalam literatur. Bahan penelitian meliputi peraturan nasional, instrumen internasional, serta literatur mengenai pengetahuan adat, keadilan epistemik, dan tata kelola lingkungan. Hasil analisis menunjukkan tiga temuan utama. Pertama, epistemologi indigenous merupakan sistem pengetahuan yang mengintegrasikan pengalaman ekologis, validasi komunal, orientasi etis-spiritual, dan transmisi antargenerasi, dengan karakteristik yang beragam sesuai konteks komunitas. Kedua, kritik epistemologi indigenous terhadap dominasi pengetahuan berpusat pada mekanisme hierarkis yang meminggirkan pemegang pengetahuan adat, tanpa mengesampingkan pentingnya pengujian ilmiah dan dialog antarsistem pengetahuan. Ketiga, pengakuan epistemik dalam hukum lingkungan memerlukan partisipasi yang bermakna, perlindungan pengetahuan adat, penilaian bukti yang kontekstual, serta mekanisme pertanggungjawaban dalam pengambilan keputusan. Berdasarkan temuan tersebut, artikel ini mengusulkan Model REKOGNISI yang terdiri atas enam dimensi, yaitu relasionalitas ontologis, ekologisitas pengetahuan, validasi komunal, orientasi etis-spiritual, transmisi antargenerasi, serta norma dan institusionalisasi. Telaah kepustakaan terhadap praktik Subak, Sasi, dan Ammatoa Kajang digunakan untuk mengeksplorasi relevansi konseptual model tersebut dalam konteks Indonesia. Kebaruan artikel ini terletak pada integrasi dimensi epistemik ke dalam kerangka analisis kelembagaan hukum lingkungan. Model REKOGNISI ditawarkan sebagai kerangka konseptual awal yang masih memerlukan validasi empiris bersama komunitas adat. Implementasinya perlu mempertimbangkan keragaman internal komunitas, hak pemegang pengetahuan, dan daya dukung ekologis guna mendorong tata kelola lingkungan yang lebih inklusif dan berkeadilan.

title: An Integrated Digital Marketing and E-Commerce Framework for Sustainable Performance: SME Perspective
summary: Background: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) face a critical gap in understanding how to systematically integrate digital marketing and e-commerce capabilities to create competitive and sustainable value. While digital transformation presents significant opportunities for SMEs, a comprehensive theoretical framework addressing both operational integration mechanisms and strategic performance outcomes within a sustainability lens remains underdeveloped in the literature.Purpose: This study develops and proposes a comprehensive theoretical framework for integrating digital marketing and e-commerce capabilities within SMEs to achieve sustainable performance, specifically addressing how these capabilities can be coordinated to influence customer experience and marketing performance among both business-to-business and business-to-consumer SMEs.Design/Methodology/Approach: This study employs a systematic literature review and conceptual synthesis (PRISMA 2020), drawing from digital business strategy, dynamic capabilities theory, and sustainable business model literature. The framework development follows a structured theoretical grounding process, integrating insights from 82 sources, comprising a core corpus of peer-reviewed journal articles and a smaller set of background references (books, seminal texts, and one standards document) across digital marketing, e-commerce, and SME strategy domains.Findings/Results: This study develops an integrated framework comprising five core components: digital marketing, e-commerce integration, technology infrastructure, organizational capabilities, and strategic capabilities, all converging toward sustainable performance. The framework identifies four integration mechanisms, namely data integration, process integration, technology integration, and customer journey integration, as proposed enablers of SME digital transformation. These mechanisms are proposed, from synthesis of the reviewed literature, to shape customer perceptions of value, trust, and journey consistency in ways that plausibly support conversion and retention. Conclusions: The framework is conceptual and requires empirical validation across different SME contexts and industries. Nevertheless, it offers SME managers, consultants, and policymakers a systematic roadmap for digital transformation, intended to guide capability development, resource allocation, and performance measurement for sustainable digital growth. It is also intended to inform SME resilience and competitiveness in digital economies.Originality/value (State of the art): Existing frameworks address single capability domains in isolation without integrating them. Prior work has identified this integration gap. This framework's distinct contribution is specifying the mechanisms through which digital marketing and e-commerce capabilities jointly shape outcomes for resource-constrained SMEs. This contribution is theoretical and, comprises propositions pending empirical testing. title: Tecnología basada en IA para el diagnóstico de la madurez de la comunicación digital de las PYMES en Cuba
summary: The digital transformation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) requires tools that can diagnose, explain, and improve communication management without relying on massive datasets or expensive infrastructures. This paper develops an artificial-intelligence (AI)-based technology for diagnosing digital communication maturity in Cuban SMEs, integrating external and internal communication, data-quality control, error detection, and algorithmic performance evaluation. The technology retains a weighted seven-indicator maturity index and adds an internal-communication module, an alert system, and an AI Quality Index (AI-QI) that is kept separate from organizational maturity. Two demonstrative SME cases, ElectroStar and FoodAlimento, are used to test arithmetic consistency and diagnostic rules from an aggregate reference matrix; they are not presented as independent empirical validation. The six recalculated IM-GPC scores were reproducible (ElectroStar: 0.209, 0.318, 0.435; FoodAlimento: 0.199, 0.241, 0.259), and a Monte Carlo analysis with ±20% perturbations of the weights showed stable classifications. The diagnostic layer is extended with schema checks, missingness, duplicate detection, logical inconsistencies, outliers, temporal leakage, data drift, model degradation, and task-specific performance metrics for classification, regression, clustering, calibration, uncertainty, and generative-AI factuality. The result is a reproducible and auditable SME-oriented procedure ready for prospective multicenter validation in Cuba.

title: Exploring Vocabularies of Motive to Optimise Patient Engagement for Drug Development
summary: Patient engagement in the drug development life cycle is becoming normalised, and the return on investment is being quantified. We sought to understand what motivates biotechnology organisations to undertake patient engagement throughout the drug development life cycle, to enable us to generate theoretically and empirically grounded knowledge to optimise patient engagement. This paper draws upon ethnographic research including 200 hours of informal observation, 50 hours of formal observation, 10 interviews with biotechnology staff and documentary analysis. With patient input throughout this research, we identified a multitude of motives for patient engagement, including regulatory requirements, corporate social responsibility and return on investment. Less evident was the translation of those motives into a framework that could optimise patient engagement over time and at scale. This was due to the dynamic nature of the drug pipeline, the limited critical space in which patient engagement can occur and misconceptions about patient engagement mechanisms, incentives and metrics. Exploring existing vocabularies of motive within an industry-led initiative identified organisational practice in both drug development processes and wider industry practices that have the potential to inhibit meaningful and sustainable engagement, and thus limit translation and optimisation of discovery-to-prescription translation for a wider group of patients.

title: Impact of Digital Technologies on the Economy, Society, and Environment
summary: Abstract A conceptual framework and a set of indicators for monitoring and evaluation of the impact of digital transformation of spheres of activity have been developed. The conceptual framework contains 4 dimensions (economic, social, environmental and institutional effects) and a set of indicators. The conceptual scheme was tested using statistical data of Rosstat for 2022, the values of indicators were calculated for all spheres of activity as a whole, as well as for organizations of specially selected spheres of activity separately. The positive impact of the use of digital technologies on the economy and social sphere was revealed, and to a lesser extent - on the environment. The most controversial impact of the use of digital technologies is on worker safety. The leaders in terms of the impact of digital development in Russia are organizations in trade and financial services.

title: From CSR Claims to Legitimacy Gaps: Abductive Topic Modeling of Fashion Communication Across the Fashion Supply Chain
summary: ABSTRACT Fiber‐Textile‐Apparel‐Retail (FTAR) firms communicate their fashion corporate social responsibility (fCSR) efforts to stakeholders to obtain operational legitimacy. However, little is known about the extent to which fCSR disclosures align with stakeholder expectations and sustainability principles. To address this gap, this study integrates legitimacy and stakeholder theories, legitimacy gaps, and the Triple Bottom Line‐Sustainable Development Goals (TBL‐SDG) framework. fCSR disclosures from 297 webpages of 80 FTAR firms were analyzed and interpreted using an abductive topic modeling approach. The results yielded three topics and six subtopics, revealing an underrepresentation of environmental sustainability. Legitimacy gaps were also identified between conformance claims and outcome evidence, stakeholder recognition and participation, and information disclosure and its evidence of usefulness, indicating that communicated fCSR remained insufficiently substantiated across legitimacy dimensions. FTAR firms can address these gaps by complementing standards, targets, and governance disclosures with verified outcomes, meaningful stakeholder participation, and evidence that disclosures provide practical benefits.

title: ESG Risk and Financial Performance in Apparel Supply Chains: Evidence from NYSE and NASDAQ Listed US Companies (2021–2024)
summary: Abstract This study investigates the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) risk and the financial performance of apparel companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the NASDAQ. The apparel industry is highly vulnerable to sustainability-related risks in its supply chains, and existing evidence on the relationship between ESG and financial performance remains fragmented and inconsistent across industries and regions. Therefore, this study examines whether the relationship between ESG and financial performance has existed in one specific market, the apparel industry, after the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a panel of 30 US-listed apparel companies observed from 2021 to 2024 (120 firm-year observations), pooled Ordinary Least Squares regression with standard errors clustered by firm was used to test the relationship between Sustainalytics' ESG Risk Score and two measures of financial performance: Return on Assets (ROA) and Net Profit Margin (NPM). The results reveal a statistically significant negative relationship between the ESG Risk Score and ROA and with NPM, respectively, suggesting that companies with a lower ESG Risk Score (better ESG Risk Management) have better financial performance. This relationship strengthens when the analysis is limited to the years 2022–2024, excluding the atypical post-pandemic recovery year of 2021, and is significant in most robustness checks, including outlier and multicollinearity tests. The results provide context-specific evidence for a body of literature with mixed findings across industries and regions, and could be relevant to apparel company managers and investors assessing the financial relevance of ESG risk management.

title: Comment Letters, Connected Investors, and Corporate Bond Issuance
summary: Using a proprietary data set that documents corporate bond issuances in China, we find that bond regulators’ comment letters (CLs) on issuers’ public disclosures generally target opaque firms and reduce bond issuance success. We also find, however, that connected investors—financial institutions with prior business relationships with the issuers—purchase a relatively larger share of bond issuances from CL recipients than from non-CL recipients, and this greater participation contributes to overpricing. Further analysis shows that connected investors support CL recipients because they possess superior private information and obtain private benefits from their connections. title: Perlindungan Hukum bagi Investor di Era Digital: Studi terhadap Penegakan Hukum oleh Otoritas Jasa Keuangan atas Maraknya Investasi Bodong, Risiko Cybersecurity, dan Aspek Hukum Financial Technology
summary: Perkembangan teknologi finansial (financial technology/fintech) telah mengubah lanskap investasi di Indonesia secara fundamental, ditandai dengan menjamurnya platform investasi berbasis digital, layanan urun dana (securities crowdfunding), serta perdagangan aset kripto berbasis blockchain. Di balik kemudahan akses tersebut, muncul pula risiko baru berupa maraknya penawaran investasi ilegal (investasi bodong), kebocoran data pribadi, dan serangan siber yang mengancam kepentingan investor. Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis bentuk penegakan hukum yang dilakukan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) melalui Satuan Tugas Pemberantasan Aktivitas Keuangan Ilegal (Satgas PASTI), pengaturan hukum terhadap risiko cybersecurity, serta aspek hukum penyelenggaraan securities crowdfunding dan pemanfaatan teknologi blockchain, ditinjau dari perspektif perlindungan hukum bagi investor. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan (statute approach) dan pendekatan konseptual (conceptual approach). Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa kerangka hukum perlindungan investor telah diperkuat melalui Undang-Undang Nomor 4 Tahun 2023 tentang Pengembangan dan Penguatan Sektor Keuangan (UU P2SK), Undang-Undang Nomor 27 Tahun 2022 tentang Pelindungan Data Pribadi, serta sejumlah Peraturan OJK, namun penegakannya masih bersifat responsif dan menghadapi tantangan yurisdiksi lintas batas, keterbatasan literasi keuangan digital masyarakat, dan cepatnya inovasi teknologi yang mendahului regulasi. Artikel ini merekomendasikan penguatan pendekatan preventif berbasis teknologi (regulatory technology), harmonisasi regulasi lintas otoritas, serta penguatan literasi dan edukasi investor sebagai bagian integral dari sistem perlindungan hukum yang komprehensif.

title: Financial Shared Services at SAIC Motor: Market Response and Outcomes
summary: Under the background of digital transformation of enterprises, the financial sharing center has gradually transformed from accounting reimbursement center to data value creation center, and the construction of financial sharing architecture of large diversified groups has become a hot spot in practice. This paper takes SAIC as a research case to explore the market performance and implementation effect of the financial sharing model of automobile manufacturing diversification group. It is found that SAIC has achieved results in reducing operating costs, strengthening capital risk management and promoting the integration of industry and finance by adopting the differentiated path of building financial sharing centers in different sectors, but at the same time, there are practical pain points such as non-uniform standards, insufficient cross-departmental coordination, redundant approval process and difficult personnel transformation. This study enriches the case study of financial sharing of automobile diversification groups and provides practical reference for similar large-scale automobile enterprises to optimize the construction of financial sharing and release the value of digital financial management.
