title: How innovation is shaped by different types CEO power
summary: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Companies undergoing digital transformation must be aware of its potential impact on how both the formal and informal power of CEOs can shape innovation. To maximize the benefits of going digital, an organization should ensure that its CEO wields enough formal authority to make and implement key decisions. It is equally imperative to enhance communication and knowledge sharing within the firm as a means of enabling leaders to build informal relationships and access the important knowledge, technologies and other resources needed to boost innovation as the digital transformation progresses. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

title: ОСНОВНІ ТЕОРІЇ ОПОДАТКУВАННЯ ТА ЇХ РОЛЬ У ФОРМУВАННІ СУЧАСНОЇ ПОДАТКОВОЇ ПОЛІТИКИ
summary: This article examines the evolution of theories of taxation and their impact on the formation of the state’s modern tax policy. It summarizes academic approaches to defining the nature and purpose of taxes, and explores the characteristics of classical tax theory, the benefit theory, the ability-to-pay theory, as well as Keynesian, monetarist, and institutional theories. It is demonstrated that modern tax policy is not based on the provisions of any single theory, but is shaped through the integration of various theoretical concepts, which ensures the fulfillment of the fiscal, regulatory, social, incentive, and control functions of taxes. A comparative analysis of the impact of major taxation theories on the formation of modern tax policy was conducted, and the specific features of their practical application in the context of the developing digital economy were identified. The interrelationship between the evolution of taxation theories, the principles of tax system design, tax policy instruments, and tax administration mechanisms was systematized. The authors propose a model for transforming tax theories into modern state tax policy, which reflects the sequence of the transition from scientific concepts to principles of taxation, the formulation of tax policy, the implementation of the tax mechanism, the conduct of tax administration, and the evaluation of the tax system’s performance. A distinctive feature of the model is that it takes into account the feedback loop between the results of tax policy implementation and the further development of theoretical approaches to taxation. A matrix has been developed to assess the impact of taxation theories on the fulfillment of the main functions of taxes, which allows for an evaluation of the extent to which individual theoretical concepts influence the fiscal, regulatory, social, incentive, and control functions of the tax system. A conceptual model for shaping modern tax policy has been proposed, combining the evolution of tax theories, the principles of tax system design, modern tax regulation tools, digital administration, and the evaluation of the tax system’s effectiveness.

title: Establishing a Sustained, Industry-Aligned Youth Technology Skills Programme in Ado-Odo/Ota Federal Constituency
summary: Policy proposal prepared for the National Youth Confab process under the Technology and Digital Innovation pillar, focused on Ado-Odo/Ota Federal Constituency, Ogun State, Nigeria. Ado-Odo/Ota is a major industrial corridor with manufacturing clusters and nearby tertiary institutions, yet many grassroots youth lack affordable, local access to digital skills training that matches industrial and remote-work demand. Existing commercial options are often costly or require travel outside the constituency. The proposal sets out a public - private partnership model for decentralised digital skills training and learn-to-work spaces within the constituency. It emphasises curriculum aligned to local manufacturing and digital economy needs, and a pathway toward preferential recruitment by participating firms. This deposit is the author’s policy submission text for public record and citation. It does not represent an adopted government programme.

title: Differences in colonial history and access to climate finance
summary: This paper investigates the empirical association of colonial history on the cross-country allocation of global climate finance. Using a 2015–2023 panel of 172 countries, we document a significant ‘colonial penalty’: formerly colonized nations receive disproportionately less climate funding. We examine three distinct mechanisms consistent with this misallocation: institutional frictions that weaken financial transparency; elevated project risks stemming from inadequate social safety nets; and infrastructural lock-in geared towards historical resource extraction, which creates logistical mismatches and raises mitigation costs. Heterogeneity analyses reveal that this negative effect is paradoxically magnified in former colonies with higher levels of income, industrialization, financial development, and corruption. These findings provide novel evidence on the deep historical roots of climate capital disparities. Given the observational nature of our data and the lack of within-country variation in colonial history, our estimates should be interpreted as robust conditional correlations rather than exact causal estimates. We highlight the need to account for historical institutional frictions in the optimal design of global climate transfers.

title: Exploring How Audit Quality Bridges the Link between Board Audit Committee Financial Expertise and Financial Reporting Quality: Empirical Evidence from Kenyan Commercial Banks
summary: Financial reporting quality (FRQ) within the banking industry is of particular interest due to the importance of transparency, market confidence and financial stability. Banks are particularly prone to FRQ issues due to the high level of estimation within the accounting process such as loan loss provisions (LLP). In addition, low FRQ may mask risk and pose a threat to financial stability. This study sought to establish the mediating effect of audit quality on the relationship between board audit committee financial expertise and financial reporting quality (FRQ) among banks in Kenya. Anchored on Agency Theory, Stakeholder Theory and Resource Dependence Theory, the study adopted a positivist philosophy and an explanatory longitudinal panel research design. Secondary data were obtained from audited financial statements, annual reports, external audit reports and Central Bank of Kenya publications covering 2015–2024, and all analyses were based on this full balanced panel of 330 observations. Financial reporting quality was measured using absolute discretionary loan-loss provisions derived from a bank-specific loan-loss-provision model, with lower values indicating less reporting discretion and higher financial reporting quality. Audit quality was proxied by external audit fees. Mediation was tested using the Sobel test. The mediation results demonstrated that audit quality mediate the relationship between financial expertise (indirect β = 0.008, p < 0.05), meeting frequency (indirect β = 0.007, p < 0.05), independence (indirect β = 0.005, p < 0.05) and size (indirect β = 0.005, p < .05) and financial reporting quality. The study recommends that banks and regulators should strengthen substantive board audit committee financial expertise and engagement between Board Audit Committees and external auditors. The findings have the potential to provide policymakers and regulators with information highlighting the significance of strong audit board committee in the process of enhancing financial reporting quality. Keywords: Quality Audit, Audit Fees, Dimensions of Board Audit Committee, Quality of Financial Reporting, Discretionary Loan-Loss Write-offs, Mediation, Kenyan Banks

title: Turning data into green action: how the environmental value of digitalization emerges in maritime supply chains
summary: As digital transformation accelerates and environmental regulations become more stringent, increasing attention has been paid to how maritime firms translate digital resources into environmental value. Drawing on organizational information processing theory and the natural resource-based view, this study develops a multistage model to examine the relationship between supply chain digitalization and environmental performance. The model focuses on an information-processing pathway reflected in supply chain visibility and a supplier-coordination pathway reflected in green supply chain collaboration, highlighting the connecting role of firms’ internal green responses. Using 253 valid questionnaire responses from Chinese maritime logistics firms, the model was tested through covariance-based structural equation modeling. The results show that supply chain digitalization is positively and significantly associated with both supply chain visibility and green supply chain collaboration, although the two capabilities exhibit distinct downstream patterns of association. Supply chain visibility is positively and significantly associated with both internal environmental management and green operational practices, whereas green supply chain collaboration is positively and significantly associated only with green operational practices; its association with internal environmental management is not statistically significant. Both internal green responses are positively and significantly associated with improvements in perceived environmental performance. These findings reveal differences in how information processing and supplier coordination connect with firms’ internal green responses, deepen the understanding of how digital resources are translated into environmental value in the maritime context, and offer practical implications for aligning digitalization initiatives with green management.

title: INVESTOR BEHAVIOUR IN THE DIGITAL FINANCIAL ECOSYSTEM: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
summary: Structured Abstract: Purpose: The aim of this study is to undertake the systematic review of academic paper on digital and financial technology to describe the impact of various digital and financial technologies on the behaviour of retail investor under several cognitive and influence their investment decision-making. The study includes internet, social media and social trading platform as a advanced communication channel and social trading application and a financial technology facilitating in execution of trading decision. Study design/methodology/approach: A systematic literature review has been conducted of 94 academic work which includes published journals, conference proceedings, working papers and published books with the systematic search of academic works from several electronic databases to identify relevant studies even though there was research work released between 2000 and 2023. The publication of notable works began in 2014. The search terms included "technological advancements," "internet," "social media," "social trading applications," "trading applications”, "retail investors," "investor behaviour," and "investment decision-making and fintech. Findings: The paper suggest that the digital and financial technological variable collectively impact investor in not only in providing with financial information but also in decision making and trade execution. The increased accessibility to information and trading avenues has led to challenges, such as information overload and the potential for overconfidence in decision-making which results in impulsive and frequent trading affecting their return. Moreover, digital communication technology such as social media, one of the essential sources of information and opinion, also is to be credited with impacting investor sentiment and behaviour leading to herd behaviour and suboptimal return. Research limitations/implications: This paper reports that investors’ behaviour post digital and financial technology adoption have high potential for further study by various stakeholders in the field of behavioural finance from academia, practitioners to regulators. Practical implications: The paper summarizes the lessons which is of importance for the retail investor, implies that retail investor should be careful in relying too much on the digital technology in terms of fetching financial information and trade execution especially when they are not financial experts. Social implications: Under this study, investors can recognize various cognitive biases that can influence their trading behavior and impact their returns. Originality/value: The paper add value in the understanding of digital and financial technological evolution and its impact, post-adoption, on the retail investors’ behaviour

title: DIGITAL SOLUTIONS FOR SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT IN HEALTHCARE
summary: Against the backdrop of the fourth revolution and the COVID-19 pandemic, many companies have started to rethink their supply chains to increase their flexibility and efficiency to ensure their 'survival'.As a result, the concept of digital supply chain has gained more attention.The concept of digital supply chain can increase the sustainability of logistics operations as it offers more tools for visualization, monitoring and forecasting.Healthcare is on the cusp of radical change into a new era of intelligent and connected healthcare called Health Care 4.0.Healthcare organizations are integrating disruptive technologies into their supply chains, ushering in the fourth industrial revolution -Healthcare Supply Chain 4.0.Healthcare Supply Chain 4.0 incorporates the sustainable practices of Industry 4.0 technologies.Thus, a comprehensive, intelligent, and interconnected healthcare society is emerging, leading to the Healthcare 4.0 paradigm.So, the aim of the study is to substantiate the relevance of the application of technological innovations in improving health care in modern times.As the methodological basis of the study, it is shown that the main goal is the transition from traditional healthcare to digital healthcare.The application of the study is to increase the effective and sustainable use of digital solutions in improving the healthcare supply chain.The findings of the study will serve to improve the healthcare supply chain, deepening the reforms on the application of high technology in this field.The originality and scientific novelty of the study is that the features and directions of application of Industry 4.0 platform components and other innovative technologies at different levels of the healthcare supply chain have been explored.

title: From resource orchestration to robustness and resilience: the role of data analytics capability in bulk commodity maritime supply chains
summary: Introduction Bulk commodity maritime supply chains are increasingly exposed to climate-related disruptions, geopolitical tensions, port congestion, transportation uncertainty, and other external shocks. However, limited attention has been paid to how firms transform dispersed supply chain resources into capabilities that support both disruption resistance and recovery. Drawing on resource orchestration theory and organizational information processing theory, this study examines how maritime supply chain resource acquisition, resource bundling, and resource leveraging are associated with data analytics capability, supply chain robustness, and supply chain resilience. Methods Survey data were collected from 214 Chinese firms substantially involved in the international seaborne import of bulk commodities. A two-wave survey design was employed, and the proposed relationships were tested using structural equation modeling. Results Resource acquisition was positively associated with resource bundling, which in turn was positively associated with resource leveraging. Resource acquisition, bundling, and leveraging were all positively associated with data analytics capability, with resource acquisition showing the strongest association. Data analytics capability was positively associated with both maritime supply chain robustness and resilience. Bootstrap analysis further identified significant indirect relationships between resource orchestration activities and disruption-response capabilities through interconnected resource orchestration processes and data analytics capability. Discussion The findings extend resource orchestration research by showing how data analytics capability is associated with the orchestration of heterogeneous and externally dispersed maritime supply chain resources. By integrating resource orchestration theory with organizational information processing theory, the study clarifies the proposed process linking resource orchestration, analytics capability, and disruption response capabilities. The findings also provide practical guidance for bulk commodity importers seeking to strengthen robustness and resilience through coordinated resource management and data-driven decision making.

title: Governance Framework and Overall Readiness for AI Enabling in Supply Chain Management in Bangladesh
summary: Digital transformation in Supply Chain Management in Bangladesh’s RMG and SME sectors has become very popular because of the need for transparency and digital compliance by foreign customers as well as demand forecasting, inventory control, logistics, traceability and operational decision-making. But most organizations could not implement Artificial Intelligence and digital technology yet. The research reviews several academic papers, industry surveys, institutional reports, government sources and other secondary sources to investigate how prepared Bangladesh is to enable, use and maintain digital technologies like Artificial Intelligence in its supply chain management and what the challenges are there. Studies suggest that high cost of implementation, insufficient number of experts, weak digital infrastructure and the unreadiness of employees and supply chain partners to adapt to a new system are the very obstacles in implementing AI not just in Supply Chain Management but also in various other departments of an organization. Other than that, big firms like export-oriented firms tend to be more prepared than SMEs in accepting advanced digital systems due to a financial and technological edge. To understand this unevenness, this research proposes a ‘Two-axis Digital Readiness Matrix’ which is based on an organization’s internal capability and digital connectivity with external supply-chain partners. This study recommends higher opportunities for financing, advancement of workforce skills, increase in management capability and digital integration among supply chain participants

title: A Study on Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Systems and Their Impact on Supply Chain Performance
summary: Businesses are increasingly using Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems for unifying the various activities that take place in their businesses and for making information accessible. This study explores the employees' perception of the efficacy of ERP in relation to supply chain performance. The focus was given to inventory management, real-time information, coordination, operating costs, procurement and information sharing. A descriptive quantitative method was used based on responses from 50 individuals. The primary data collection tool was a structured questionnaire that consisted of questions about respondent's characteristics, the usage of ERP in business and supply chain performance. The performance was assessed through different statements using a five-point scale, and the analysis of the data was conducted using percentages. According to the results, generally, the perceptions were positive. Nearly 80% of the respondents think that ERP improves the efficiency of inventory management, and 76% confirmed that it provides them with accurate real-time information. 66% agreed that they can achieve better coordination in the work of departments, while 74% of the respondents confirmed that ERP reduces the operating costs. The research shows that respondents participate in such ERP usage on a regular basis. In sum, the results demonstrate that ERP systems provide greater visibility of information along with improved inventory tasks, procurement processes, and supply chain collaboration. More frequent training, upgraded systems, secure data management, support for users, analytic techniques, employee participation, and standardized processes can enhance the effectiveness of ERP use. title: Effect of Accruals Quality on the Firm Value of Construction and Allied Firms Listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: Accruals quality is a dimension of financial reporting quality because reliable accrual information enables investors to assess reported earnings and firm performance. However, evidence on whether accruals quality translates into higher firm value remains limited among construction and allied firms listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange. The study examined the effect of accruals quality on firm value. It was anchored on Signalling Theory, which explains how credible financial information provides useful signals to market participants. A causal research design was adopted using panel data from four firms with financial information covering 2015–2025. Accruals quality was measured using the Dechow and Dichev (2002) model, while firm value was measured using Tobin’s Q. Panel regression analysis was conducted using STATA Version 18, with the hypothesis tested at the 5% significance level. The findings showed that accruals quality had a positive and statistically significant effect on firm value (β = 1.428, p = .003). This finding indicates that higher-quality accrual information was associated with higher market valuation among the sampled construction and allied firms. The study concluded that accruals quality was an important financial reporting attribute in explaining firm value within the sector. It recommended that firms strengthen accounting systems, internal controls, audit oversight, and financial reporting practices to improve the reliability of accrual information. Future research should examine whether audit quality, corporate governance, ownership structure, and investor information processing explain the relationship between accruals quality and firm value

title: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES FOR SUPPORTING STRATEGIC DECISIONS TO ENSURE THE OMNI-RESILIENCE OF THE DEVELOPMENT BUSINESS
summary: The digital transformation of the development business necessitates an integrated information and analytical environment for strategic management, capable of ensuring rapid data processing, forecasting the consequences of management alternatives, and maintaining enterprise resilience amid dynamic changes in the environment. Digital support for strategic decision-making rests on the interaction of BIM, ERP, CRM, BI, and DSS systems, which consolidate project, financial, operational, marketing, and management information within a unified digital space. The article aims to establish how the integration of BIM, ERP, CRM, BI, and DSS systems within a unified information and analytical environment affects the strategic effectiveness and omni-resilience of the development business.The methodological basis comprises structural and functional analysis, mathematical formalisation and integral assessment, a multi-criteria approach accounting for data quality, interoperability and the speed of information exchange, and comparative analysis of digital environment parameters.The functional role of digital technologies is identified, and the dependence of their strategic effectiveness on data quality, interoperability, the speed of information exchange, and the level of digital environment integration is established. A multi-level architecture of digital support for management decisions is proposed, combining data sources, cross-system integration, analytical processing, and strategic decision formation. An assessment system is developed, based on indicators of digital integration, analytical efficiency, response speed, and strategic effectiveness. A closed-loop adaptive management framework is substantiated, ensuring model updating and adjustment of strategic parameters.The strategic reserve for the development of digital technologies amounts to 34.3%. The forecast results demonstrate an increase in the digital support effectiveness index to 0.694, the digital environment integration coefficient to 0.647, the strategic decision effectiveness index to 0.828, the level of analytical performance to 0.735, and the level of omni-resilience to 0.692, confirming the effectiveness of digital technologies in ensuring the competitiveness of the development business.

title: МЕТОДИЧНИЙ ПІДХІД ДО ІНТЕГРАЦІЇ СТРАТЕГІЧНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ ЛЮДСЬКИМ КАПІТАЛОМ У СИСТЕМУ БІЗНЕС-ПЛАНУВАННЯ ПІДПРИЄМСТВА
summary: Human resource management is crucial for achieving company goals, as it supports the strategic direction, development and motivation of employees in order to ensure the long-term competitiveness and success of the company. The article examines the theoretical and methodological principles of integrating strategic human capital management into the business planning system of an enterprise in the context of the digital transformation of the economy, increased global competition and the growing role of intangible assets in the formation of long-term competitive advantages. It is substantiated that traditional approaches to business planning do not sufficiently take into account the strategic potential of human capital, considering staffing mainly as an element of the organizational plan, which limits the possibilities of effective use of the intellectual resources of the enterprise. Based on the systemic, process, competency and strategic approaches, the author's methodological approach to integrating strategic human capital management into the business planning system of the enterprise has been developed. The proposed approach is based on the consistent integration of the personnel strategy into all functional components of the business plan, including marketing, production, organizational, financial and investment sections, as well as the risk management system. A conceptual model for integrating strategic human capital management into business planning has been developed, the main stages of its implementation have been identified, a system of key performance indicators has been formed, an organizational and economic mechanism for monitoring performance and adaptive adjustment of management decisions has been proposed. A feature of the proposed approach is the focus on the continuous development of human capital as a key factor in implementing the enterprise's strategy, increasing its innovative capacity, digital maturity and competitiveness. The practical value of the proposed approach lies in the possibility of its use when developing business plans for enterprises of various types of economic activity, forming strategic personnel development programs, improving personnel policy and making management decisions regarding investment in human capital.

title: Evolution of Crisis Communication: Exploring Organizational Perceptions and Social Media Adoption in Vietnam’s Dynamic Digital Landscape
summary: This paper explores the evolving role of social media in crisis communication within the Vietnamese context, applying a comparative methodology to analyze data collected over two distinct time periods. By comparing findings from interviews conducted in 2018 and 2023, the study offers unique insights into the shifting perceptions of public relations practitioners regarding the use of social media in crisis management. This comparative approach not only highlights temporal changes but also enriches existing theoretical frameworks, particularly the Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory, by considering how media characteristics and cultural factors influence the adoption of social media in non-European crisis contexts. The study further contributes to the understanding of crisis communication by examining how these dynamics operate in a rapidly developing, non-Western nation like Vietnam, where digital transformation and social media usage are burgeoning. This work provides valuable lessons for scholars and practitioners alike, offering a deeper understanding of how social media can be more effectively integrated into crisis communication strategies in diverse cultural environments.

title: Institutional Quality and the Financial Returns of Social Supply Chain Practices
summary: ABSTRACT Social supply chain practices (SSCP) have become increasingly relevant as firms seek to support sustainable development and respond to stakeholder expectations. This study examines the association between SSCP and corporate financial performance (CFP) and investigates the moderating role of country‐level institutional quality. Drawing on resource dependence, legitimacy, and institutional theories, we constructed a composite SSCP index based on 11 binary indicators and applied fixed‐effects panel regressions to global firm‐level data from 2018 to 2023. The results show that SSCP is negatively associated with return on assets (ROA) and Tobin's Q , while their association with market capitalization is not statistically significant. The interaction between SSCP and country‐level institutional quality is positive and significant across all three CFP measures, indicating that the estimated SSCP–CFP association becomes more favorable as institutional quality increases. However, the conditional pattern differs across the three CFP measures. For market capitalization, the association becomes positive and statistically significant at high levels of institutional quality, whereas for ROA and Tobin's Q , it becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero and does not become significantly positive within the observed range. Thus, by combining a social‐specific measure of supply chain practices, multiple dimensions of CFP, and country‐level institutional quality in a global sample, this study provides a more integrated examination of the SSCP–CFP association. These findings show that the SSCP–CFP association varies across financial measures and institutional governance contexts, highlighting country‐level institutional quality as an important boundary condition in this association.

title: CEO Career Horizon, Firm Age, and Market Value Growth: Determinants of Corporate Sustainability
summary: ABSTRACT The aim of this investigation is to expand the understanding of the effect of chief executive officer (CEO) horizon on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices using an unbalanced panel data set of Saudi‐listed companies from 2016 to 2024. This study provides new evidence that CEOs' approach to retirement has a positive and significant impact on environmental, social, and governance practices. Two justifications support these findings: first, CEOs may seek to protect their legacy and reputation before leaving their position; second, the Saudi Capital Market Authority encourages listed companies to produce annual ESG reports by providing public guidelines for ESG. Additionally, our study finds that firm size and firm age are positively and significantly associated with environmental, governance, and social disclosures. It also reveals a significant positive relationship between firm growth and environmental and governance disclosures, while no significant association is found between firm growth and social disclosures. The results are robust to various tests and alternative explanations.

title: An Analysis of Tesla's Supply Chain Management Model
summary: As the global new energy vehicle (NEV) industry enters a phase of stock competition and high-quality development, supply chain management capabilities, cost optimization levels, and resilience to supply chain risks have become key sources of competitive differentiation among automakers, fundamentally changing the traditional automotive industry's emphasis on scale-based competition. Tesla, as a benchmark enterprise in the global NEV industry, has established a new supply chain management system that is underpinned by digitalization, features vertical integration as its core barrier, and integrates global layout with localized adaptation and coordination. The model also incorporates multiple supply sources and production locations to diversify supply chain risks. This paper takes Tesla's supply chain management model as the research object, systematically analyzing its core supply chain characteristics from three major frameworks: upstream supplier layout, midstream independent manufacturing of core technologies, and downstream direct-to-consumer (D2C) services. Additionally, it examines the practical challenges faced by Tesla's supply chain in the context of current global geopolitical conflicts, overseas policy barriers, and fluctuations in mineral resources. The study finds that the core advantages of Tesla's supply chain model lie in eliminating information silos across the entire chain through digital technology, gaining control over costs and technology through independent research and production in core areas, and achieving cost reduction, efficiency improvement, and risk diversification through a globally dispersed layout and deep localization adaptation. However, the model also has limitations, including limited resilience to supply disruptions resulting from a streamlined supplier base and substantial exposure to foreign-market policy changes.

title: Contractual Absolution: A Legal-Economic Framework Restricting Extra-Contractual Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in State-Subsidized Enterprises
summary: Contemporary political economy frequently imposes open-ended Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) demands on private firms that receive state subsidies, public grants, or regulatory concessions. This paper establishes the legal-economic doctrine of Contractual Absolution. We argue that when a private enterprise enters into a bilateral subsidy agreement with the state and fulfills its explicitly stipulated Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)—such as job creation targets, capital expenditure quotas, or technological benchmarks—its legal and moral obligations to the state are fully discharged. Imposing extra-contractual social expectations post hoc violates administrative principles of non-arbitrariness, increases regulatory risk, and enables state institutions to shift public policy failures onto private balance sheets. By integrating Transaction Cost Economics and the Administrative Principle of Prohibition of Improper Coupling, this framework establishes that strict contractual performance grants complete immunity from extralegal moral demands, reclaiming transaction realism in state-firm governance.

title: Tracing working capital pressure in concentrated supply chains with temporal graph transformers
summary: Concentrated trading relationships can improve coordination, yet they can also amplify operational stress when inventories, delivery commitments, and short-term obligations become misaligned. Conventional concentration ratios summarize dependence at the firm level but reveal little about how this pressure develops over time or travels through multi-tier supplier–buyer relations. This study presents SC-GraphTransformer-Press, a temporal graph framework that combines upstream and downstream concentration, product-specific transaction structure, recurrent firm states, and attention-based propagation to forecast working capital pressure. Pressure is operationalized as an inventory-backed stress proxy derived from unmet inventory-related obligations and available inventory, with firm-scale and network controls used to distinguish firms that have similar relative pressure but different operating capacities. The forecasting experiments use three SupplySim-derived benchmarks in which the required inventory and backlog states are observable. Under chronological multi-horizon evaluation, the proposed model achieves the strongest predictive performance among econometric, machine-learning, static graph, and temporal graph baselines, with its advantage increasing at longer horizons and under supply disruption. Network diagnostics further associate concentrated dependencies with persistent downstream pressure, while model-based scenarios indicate that supplier exits and supply shocks produce larger predicted responses than customer concentration and that product substitution can moderate these responses. Chronological audits and robustness tests across concentration assignments, shock locations, and simulator settings support the stability of these findings. The framework therefore offers a practical route from static concentration measurement to forward-looking diagnosis of working capital stress in dynamic supply-chain networks.

title: Teaching Generation Z: The Pedagogical Innovation Pentagon For Hybrid Introductory Marketing Education
summary: This study examines how pedagogical innovation can support Generation Z students in post-COVID marketing education, where hybrid learning and artificial intelligence are reshaping course design. It introduces the Pedagogical Innovation Pentagon, an evidence-informed model organized around five interrelated dimensions: hybridization, digitalization, artificial intelligence, responsibility, and harmonization. The model was developed and evaluated through a mixed-methods exploratory study conducted with first-year students enrolled in a bilingual introductory marketing course within a multi-campus business program. The model was implemented through an Instructional Capsule, a structured learning environment combining bilingual content development, guided activities, feedback mechanisms, sustainability-focused case studies, and shared assessment practices across campuses. Student self-reports and course analytics were used to explore how this instructional approach supported engagement, clarity, feedback, ethical awareness, and coherence in students’ learning experiences. Findings suggest that effective innovation in marketing education depends less on technological sophistication than on the meaningful integration of digital tools within a human-centered and ethically intentional learning environment. The study contributes to marketing education by offering a transferable approach for integrating digital transformation, AI, and responsible pedagogy into course design and continuous improvement.

title: Analisis Peran Literasi Keuangan dan Adopsi Teknologi Keamanan dalam Menunjang Keberhasilan UMKM
summary: This study analyzes the role of financial literacy and security technology adoption in supporting the success of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). Digital transformation provides opportunities for market expansion, transaction efficiency, and better access to financial services, but it also increases exposure to digital security risks such as transaction fraud, data misuse, phishing, customer data leakage, and improper use of financial technology. This article applies a conceptual study approach through a narrative literature review by integrating financial literacy, the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, and the Resource-Based View (RBV). The review indicates that financial literacy enhances MSME owners’ capability to prepare budgets, manage cash flow, select financial products, assess risks, and make business investment decisions. Meanwhile, security technology adoption serves as a mechanism to protect digital assets and customer trust through multi-factor authentication, encryption, data backup, system updates, access control, and cybersecurity education. The synergy between financial literacy and security technology forms digital-financial capability that strengthens MSME success in terms of financial performance, operational efficiency, business sustainability, and reputation. This article proposes a conceptual model and research propositions for future empirical testing.

title: AI-Driven Consumer Behaviour Analytics: Transforming Retail and Marketing Practices in Tamil Nadu, India
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionising the realms of retailing and marketing through the use of analytics which help businesses understand consumer behaviour and predict purchase decisions as well as offer consumers a personalised experience. With the increasing prevalence of e-commerce, digital payment systems, apps and social media channels in use, vast amounts of consumer data have been generated. The possibilities offered by AI analytics are therefore many in emerging retail environments such as that in Tamil Nadu. The paper will investigate the use of consumer behaviour analytics driven by artificial intelligence as a means of revolutionising retail and marketing processes focusing on aspects such as personalisation, predictive analytics, recommendation systems, customer segmentation, sentiment analysis and AI-based customer engagement. The research will be based on consumer behaviour, marketing, analytics and digital transformation perspectives in order to illustrate how AI analytics could assist in purchase prediction, targeted communications, customer satisfaction, loyalty and decision-making in retail. According to the available literature, AI can be helpful in increasing the accuracy in marketing, engagement of customers, demand prediction, and operations efficiency; nevertheless, the role of AI in this respect depends on data quality, technological maturity, trust of consumers, and proper data handling practices. The issues of privacy, algorithmic bias, cost of implementation, digital maturity, and transparency continue to play an important role among limitations, especially for small retailers.

title: The management paradigm transformation in pharmacy: from traditional models to the use of digital technologies
summary: The relevance of the study is due to the impact of digitalization and crisis factors on the pharmaceutical sector, which determines the need for a theoretical rethinking of the modern management paradigm in pharmacy. Aim. To theoretically substantiate the evolution of the management paradigm in pharmacy, identify the main stages of its transformation, and systematize the characteristics of the contemporary digital management model of pharmaceutical organizations. Materials and methods. The information base for this study was compiled from regulatory and strategic documents (WHO, Ministry of Health of Ukraine) and scientific publications for 2015–2026, retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar using keywords related to digitalization and management in pharmacy. The study used systemic, structural and functional, comparative, and historical-logical methods, as well as generalization and scientific abstraction. Results and discussion. Six stages in the evolution of the management paradigm in pharmacy, such as administrative-functional, economic-market, strategic, process-oriented, patient-centered, and digital stage, have been systematized. It has been substantiated that each subsequent paradigm does not eliminate the previous one, but transforms and integrates its managerial tools in accordance with changing conditions in the pharmaceutical sector. The transition from managing resources, functions, and operations to managing end-to-end processes, relationships, data, digital platforms, as well as ecosystems, has been identified. The transformation of managerial functions from periodic planning, control, and experience-based decision-making towards dynamic forecasting, real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, automation, and data-driven decision-making has been demonstrated. The social-pharmaceutical dimension of the digital paradigm has been substantiated, within which the digital transformation contributes to improving the accessibility and quality of pharmaceutical care, strengthening patient-centredness, and increasing the social efficiency of pharmaceutical organizations. The need to combine technological efficiency with risk management, cybersecurity, human capital development, and digital resilience has been determined. Conclusions. Digitalization is defined as a systemic transformation of the management paradigm that provides the transition from a predominantly hierarchical and reactive model to an adaptive, process-oriented, network-based, platform, and data-driven management model. Further research should focus on developing methodological approaches to assessing the digital maturity and digital resilience of pharmaceutical organizations, identifying appropriate KPIs, and studying their relationship with the quality of pharmaceutical care and social effectiveness.

title: Impact of artificial intelligence on project planning, scheduling, and control
summary: Abstract The growing complexity of engineering and construction projects has revealed the weaknesses of conventional project planning, scheduling, and control approaches. Traditional tools often employ fixed assumptions, deterministic models, and past averages, which are inadequate for dealing with uncertainty, dynamic environments, and large-scale data. Artificial intelligence has become a disruptive technology that can be used to improve decision-making, prediction, and automation in project management processes. This paper examines the application of artificial intelligence in project planning, scheduling, and control within the engineering and construction sector. The paper summarises the application of artificial intelligence methods, including machine learning, optimization algorithms, and predictive analytics, in enhancing project performance using a methodical review of the recent scholarly literature and industry practise. The results show that artificial intelligence promotes the planning accuracy, flexibility of scheduling, and real-time project control to a great extent, as it allows data-driven insights and flexible responses. Issues of data quality, company preparedness, and ethical issues are major obstacles to implementation. The research paper adds to the project management literature because it develops the application of artificial intelligence in the three fundamental project management functions and provides practical advice to practitioners interested in introducing intelligent project management systems. Keywords Artificial intelligence, project planning, project scheduling, project control, construction management, digital transformation

title: EFFECT OF STRATEGIC PLANNING ON PERFORMANCE OF SELECTED SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES IN NASARAWA STATE, NIGERIA
summary: The persistent performance challenges confronting SMEs in Nasarawa State, despite ongoing government enterprise development initiatives, are compounded by the absence of rigorous, construct-level SMEs in the state. On the above problem study examines the effect of strategic planning on the performance of selected Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Nasarawa State, Nigeria. The study specifically investigates the effects of technological trends and strategy formulation on SME performance. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, and primary data were collected from 241 valid respondents comprising owners/managers of registered SMEs in Nasarawa State. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) version 3.5 was employed for data analysis, following a two-stage assessment of the measurement and structural models. The structural model findings revealed technological trends has a positive and significant effect on SME performance. While, strategy formulation exerts a negative and insignificant effect on SME performance. These findings establish technology-responsive strategic planning as the dominant driver of SME performance in Nasarawa State, while revealing that conventional, analytically intensive strategy formulation processes do not generate measurable performance improvements in this context. The study recommends technology-embedded strategic planning, adaptive and lean strategy approaches, and deliberate policy support for SME digital transformation in Nasarawa State

title: An Analysis of the Use of the Simlinmas Application as an Innovation in Digital Reporting on Public Order and Safety
summary: The government is exploring digital innovations in public service delivery, particularly in maintaining public order and safety, in response to advancements in information technology. One such innovation is the Simlinmas application, a digital platform for reporting public order and safety issues. This study aims to examine the use of the Simlinmas application as an e-government-based innovation in public service delivery, identify the factors influencing its adoption, and evaluate its contribution to enhancing public participation and service effectiveness. This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach using secondary data obtained through a literature review. The analysis is guided by Everett M. Rogers' (2003) Diffusion of Innovations Theory. The findings indicate that the Simlinmas application offers several advantages over conventional reporting systems, particularly in terms of reporting speed, accessibility, and transparency in report follow-up procedures. From the perspective of innovation diffusion attributes, the primary factors influencing adoption are ease of use (complexity), compatibility with community needs, and perceived benefits (relative advantage). However, disparities in digital literacy, insufficient public outreach initiatives, and inconsistent institutional responses to submitted reports remain significant barriers to adoption. These findings suggest that the Simlinmas application represents a relevant and strategic innovation that supports the digital transformation of public order and safety services. To optimize its utilization, it is essential to expand public outreach and digital literacy initiatives, strengthen data security measures, and reinforce the government's commitment to providing timely, transparent, and accountable responses to all reports received.

title: Balancing Majority Rule and Minority Protection under the Companies Act, 2013: A Critical Study
summary: The principle of majority rule is one of the fundamental principles of company law. A company, being an artificial legal person, functions through collective decision-making by its shareholders and directors. Ordinarily, decisions supported by the majority of shareholders are respected because the efficient functioning of a company requires a workable system of democratic corporate decision-making. However, unrestricted majority rule may result in the abuse of corporate power and prejudice the legitimate interests of minority shareholders. Minority shareholders may face exclusion from management, unfair allotment of shares, dilution of voting rights, diversion of corporate assets, denial of information, improper related-party transactions and other forms of oppressive conduct. The Companies Act, 2013 seeks to establish a balance between majority rule and minority protection. Sections 241 to 244 provide a statutory framework for the prevention of oppression and mismanagement, while Section 245 provides a mechanism for class action. The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has been entrusted with significant remedial powers to bring an end to oppressive or prejudicial conduct. Section 244 also permits the Tribunal to waive the prescribed eligibility requirements in appropriate cases. This paper critically examines the relationship between majority rule and minority protection under the Companies Act, 2013. It analyses the judicial development of the principles of oppression, mismanagement, legitimate corporate purpose and fair treatment, with particular reference to Shanti Prasad Jain v. Kalinga Tubes Ltd., Needle Industries (India) Ltd. v. Needle Industries Newey (India) Holding Ltd., Dale & Carrington Investment (P) Ltd. v. P.K. Prathapan, Sangramsinh P. Gaekwad v. Shantadevi P. Gaekwad and Tata Consultancy Services Ltd. v. Cyrus Investments Pvt. Ltd. The paper argues that Indian company law has moved from an exclusively majoritarian approach towards a more balanced model of corporate governance. Nevertheless, difficulties relating to access to remedies, proof of oppression, procedural delays and the distinction between legitimate business decisions and oppressive conduct continue to affect the effectiveness of minority protection. The paper concludes that minority protection should be strengthened without undermining legitimate managerial autonomy and the principle of majority decision-making.

title: ОПЕРАЦІЙНА СИСТЕМА СЕРВІСНОЇ ОРГАНІЗАЦІЇ: ІНТЕГРАЦІЯ ФУНКЦІОНАЛЬНОЇ СТРУКТУРИ ТА БІЗНЕС-ПРОЦЕСНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ
summary: The article explores the theoretical and methodological principles of forming the operating system of a service organization in the context of digital transformation of the economy and process-oriented management. The incompatibility of traditional functional management models, built only on the division of the organization into structural divisions, with the requirements of modern service business is substantiated. It is substantiated that the modern operating system of a service organization should be considered not as a set of separate functional units, but as an integrated system of interconnected business processes aimed at creating value for the consumer. The need to integrate digital technologies, business process automation systems and analytical tools into the functioning of the operating system of a service organization is confirmed. The features of service organizations that determine the specifics of building their operating systems are determined. The essence of the operating system of a service organization as an open socio-economic system that combines basic, supporting and management business processes in a single information and organizational space is revealed. Particular attention is paid to modern concepts of process management, digitalization of business processes, the use of international quality management standards, and the principles of Business Process Management (BPM). The architecture of the operating system of a service organization based on the business process approach is proposed, the mechanism of functioning of the operating system of a service organization in the conditions of business process management, the author's typology of business processes of the operating system of a service organization by levels of value creation. A comparative characteristic of the functional-hierarchical and business process approaches to managing a service organization is provided. A conceptual model of the operating system of a service organization as an integration of the functional structure and business process management is formed, which can be used by managers of service enterprises to improve operational management.

title: Consumer Behavior of Digital Payment Usage in Online Food Delivery Services
summary: Abstract: The rapid development of technologies has influenced the food delivery market significantly by changing the process of ordering food. Nowadays, the worldwide online food delivery market has been growing rapidly due to the wide spread of smartphones and the emergence of digital platforms, making it easier for customers to order food on any occasion. This research aims to explore the impact of digitalization on online food delivery services and find the reasons for their success. Digitalization tools such as mobile applications, online payments, order tracking, and recommendations help customers to order food conveniently and enjoy their experience. In addition, data analytics and artificial intelligence allow online platforms to optimize their logistics, delivery time, and marketing strategies. The transition into digital technology also brought about new business models like cloud kitchens and virtual restaurants, which are disrupting the manner in which people consume food through greater flexibility, affordability, and choice. This paper investigates the effects of digital platforms, mobile technology, and social media on consumer behavior and preferences in the online food delivery industry. In addition, the paper brings to light some of the opportunities and challenges that key stakeholders like food delivery service providers, restaurants, and policymakers face in response to the rapidly evolving digital environment. Digital technologies are vital in ensuring competitiveness and efficiency within the online food delivery industry. title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in African Academic Libraries: Opportunities, Constraints, and a Framework for Context-Sensitive Implementation
summary: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is transforming scholarly communication and knowledge-sharing practices in academic libraries worldwide. However, academic libraries in Nigeria and other African contexts continue to experience challenges related to limited visibility of research outputs, fragmented dissemination systems, uneven institutional repository development, information overload, and restricted access to scholarly resources. This paper presents a conceptual and analytical review of the strategic role of AI in strengthening scholarly communication and knowledge-sharing practices in African academic libraries. Drawing on recent scholarly literature, policy documents, and conceptual perspectives on digital transformation, the study examines the application of emerging AI technologies, including machine learning, natural language processing, recommender systems, and research analytics tools, in enhancing knowledge organisation, research discovery, open access integration, repository visibility, collaboration, and research evaluation. The paper further analyses contextual barriers affecting AI adoption, including inadequate digital infrastructure, funding limitations, professional capacity gaps, algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, and weak institutional policy frameworks. Based on these analyses, the paper proposes a context-sensitive AI adoption framework that integrates technological readiness, institutional capacity, ethical governance, and policy support as essential dimensions for sustainable scholarly communication transformation. The paper concludes that strategic investment in digital infrastructure, librarian capacity development, inclusive data governance, and coordinated institutional policies is critical for ensuring that AI contributes to equitable, accessible, and sustainable knowledge-sharing ecosystems in African academic environments.

title: Farmers market as public quick commerce infrastructure: a conceptual policy framework for digital transformation
summary: The rapid digitalization of food retail through private quick commerce platforms has transformed urban food consumption patterns in India. Despite the investments in digital infrastructure, Uzhavar Sandhai (Farmers Market), a farmer-to-consumer direct marketing system in Tamil Nadu, is still limited to traditional physical markets. This study suggests a strategic rethinking of Farmers Market as a public quick commerce infrastructure layer, incorporating digital marketplaces, hyperlocal logistics and cooperative governance to boost farmer market competitiveness and promote public value, food system resilience and equitable digital market access. In this study, the Farmers Market Digital Platform model is developed by applying the conceptual policy design approach to convert the Farmers Market platform into a decentralized public quick commerce network. This study identifies the institutional, technological and governance reforms necessary to support the digital transformation of farmer markets using publicly governed digital infrastructure. This reorientation of Farmers Market to public digital infrastructure could form the policy roadmap for platformization of agriculture in Tamil Nadu, which would benefit small farmers, urban consumers, and municipalities and help alleviate inefficiencies in supply chains. As a conceptual policy framework, the proposed model has not been empirically tested and requires future pilot implementation and validation before adoption. The study contributes to the evolving literature on agricultural digitalization by offering a vision for the potential redesign of existing public agricultural markets as digitally enabled public service infrastructure, which can enhance farmer welfare and urban food system resilience.

title: РОЛЬ ФІНАНСОВОГО МЕНЕДЖМЕНТУ В ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННІ ЕФЕКТИВНОСТІ ОПЕРАЦІЙНОЇ ДІЯЛЬНОСТІ ІТ-КОМПАНІЇ В УМОВАХ ПОСИЛЕНОЇ ЦИФРОВІЗАЦІЇ ЕКОНОМІКИ
summary: At the current stage of societal development, information technologies and the economy are closely interconnected, giving rise to new business models, digital markets, value creation mechanisms, and forms of customer interaction. The IT sector is regarded not merely as an economic sector but as an infrastructural foundation for the digital transformation of all areas of economic activity, where information and digital technologies have become key economic resources. Accordingly, issues related to providing systematic support for the operations of IT companies and creating a favorable environment for their sustainable development are becoming increasingly relevant. Financial management plays an important role in ensuring such support. The purpose of this article is to examine the role of financial management in ensuring the operational efficiency of IT companies amid intensified digitalization of the economy. In the course of the research, a set of general scientific and specialized methods was employed, including the system analysis method to summarize theoretical approaches to interpreting the concept of “financial management”; the conceptualization method to formulate the author’s definition of the term “financial management in IT”; comparison and scientific generalization methods to examine the specific features of financial management in the IT industry and contemporary approaches to improving companies’ operational efficiency through the mechanisms by which financial management influences operational activities; and the logical generalization method to formulate conclusions and practical recommendations. The article systematizes approaches to interpreting the essence of the term “financial management,” distinguishing three main approaches: process-based, resource-based, and systems-based. An author’s interpretation of the concept of “financial management in IT” is proposed. The key features of financial management for enterprises in the IT industry are identified. A scheme illustrating the relationship between financial management and the operational activities of an IT company is developed. The feasibility of applying financial management as an effective tool for improving the operational efficiency of an IT company is substantiated.

title: Contribution of Stakeholders to the Construction of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in the Forest Industry Sector in the Congo Basin: An Experience Rooted in the Cameroonian Context
summary: This experimental study aims to deepen current knowledge on the contribution of stakeholders in building corporate social responsibility, particularly in the forest industry sector in the Congo Basin. To our knowledge, no study has yet done so, at least empirically in our context. We conceptualize the process of stakeholder contribution in the construction of corporate social responsibility from a multiple case study, in this case three logging companies in Cameroon, the first of which obtained a forest certification label, the second is in the process of obtaining the same label and the third which is hostile to any labeling process. From the analysis of the studied cases follow the managerial recommendations of the research that are discussed, the limitations noted and the future directions of the research are suggested.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Economic and Financial Communication: Challenges, Practices, and Perspectives for More Transparent and Efficient Information
summary: In a context of accelerated digital transformation, this article examines the extent to which and the conditions under which artificial intelligence (AI) transforms economic and financial communication by improving information quality, transparency, and decision-making efficiency. Drawing on agency theory, information asymmetry, and information governance, it proposes a conceptual model articulating a chain of relationships whereby AI influences information quality, which in turn shapes transparency, ultimately improving decision-making performance, while also integrating a direct effect of AI on that performance and a risk of algorithmic opacity. The model further incorporates moderating variables: information governance arrangements, data quality, and the complementarity between human expertise and intelligent systems, resulting in eight research hypotheses covering both direct and moderating effects across the model. An exploratory qualitative study, based on semi-structured interviews with twenty-three professionals from the public and private sectors, conducted either in person or remotely and processed through thematic analysis, shows that AI is predominantly perceived as a lever for automation, reliability, and decision support, particularly through the reduction of human errors and the processing of massive data volumes. However, these effects remain conditional upon the quality of input data, adequate governance arrangements, and the maintenance of human oversight, while risks of algorithmic opacity, bias, hallucinations, and confidentiality persist, alongside a structural lag in adoption within the public sector. The article therefore supports a contingent, non-techno-deterministic understanding of AI in economic and financial communication, in which technological value added remains subordinate to data quality, governance, and human intervention rather than to the technology itself.

title: Corporate social responsibility shapes organizational citizenship behavior among gen Z: the role of pride, engagement and person–organization fit
summary: Purpose This study analyzes how corporate social responsibility (CSR) – including internal CSR, CSR toward the community, CSR toward customers, and CSR toward the government – affects the organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) of Generation Z employees in Vietnam. It focuses on uncovering the psychological mechanisms through which CSR is translated into OCB via employees' organizational pride (EOP) and employee engagement (ENG), while also testing the moderating role of person–organization fit (POF). Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 340 Generation Z employees working in enterprises across various sectors such as information technology, finance–banking, e-commerce, manufacturing, and marketing–communications in Vietnam. The study employed PLS-SEM technique using SmartPLS 4 to test the research hypotheses. Findings The results reveal that CSR positively influences EOP and ENG, thereby fostering OCB. Notably, the study identifies the independent mediating roles of EOP and ENG in the CSR–OCB relationship. Furthermore, ENG serves as an additional mediator linking organizational pride to OCB. The findings also confirm that POF strengthens the effects of CSR, organizational pride, and ENG on organizational citizenship behavior. Originality/value This study contributes to the employee-level CSR literature by demonstrating that CSR is not merely a managerial practice but is interpreted by Generation Z employees as a signal of organizational values and identity. It clarifies the psychological process through which CSR perceptions are transformed into OCB via sequential psychological responses involving organizational pride and ENG. Moreover, the study identifies POF as a critical boundary condition that enhances the effectiveness of CSR in promoting positive employee behaviors.

title: Pengaruh Accrual Earnings Management dan ESG disclosure terhadap Capital Structure: Studi pada Perusahaan Non-keuangan yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: Studi ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh accrual earnings management dan ESG disclosure terhadap capital structure di perusahaan non-keuangan yang terdaftar di BEI periode 2020-2024. Studi ini mempergunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder dan teknik purposive sampling. Analisis dilaksanakan mempergunakan regresi linear. Temuan studi ini memperlihatkan bahwasanya accrual earnings management dan ESG disclosure dapat memengaruhi signifikan negatif terhadap capital structure. Temuan tersebut memperlihatkan bahwasanya perusahaan yang menerapkan manajemen laba serta mempunyai tingkat pengungkapan ESG lebih tinggi cenderung mempunyai tingkat leverage lebih rendah. Studi ini memberikan bukti empiris yang dapat memperkaya literatur bidang akuntansi dan keuangan, sekaligus menjadi bahan pertimbangan bagi perusahaan menetapkan kebijakan pendanaan optimal. Implikasi penelitian menunjukkan pentingnya transparansi informasi dan kualitas pelaporan keuangan dalam mendukung Keputusan pendanaan. Hasil penelitian ini juga dapat menjadi referensi bagi investor, manajemen, dan pemangku kepentingan dalam mengevaluasi risiko keuangan, tata kelola, serta strategi perusahaan secara lebih komprehensif dan berkelanjutan untuk menghadapi perubahan lingkungan bisnis global.

title: СТРАТЕГІЧНІ ПРІОРИТЕТИ РОЗВИТКУ КАДРОВОГО ПОТЕНЦІАЛУ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ В УМОВАХ ЦИФРОВИХ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЙ
summary: The article examines the strategic development of enterprise human resource potential in the context of digital transformations. The impact of digitalization, automation and artificial intelligence on competency requirements and human resource management is considered. It is substantiated that technological changes require enterprises to shift from responding mainly to current staffing needs towards the proactive development of human resource capabilities aligned with strategic objectives and prospective competency needs. The strategic priorities for human resource potential development are systematized, including the development of professional, digital and managerial competencies, employee upskilling and reskilling, internal mobility, talent pool formation, recruitment of specialists with scarce competencies, and digitalization of HR processes. It is determined that the choice and combination of these priorities should depend on strategic competency gaps and the prospective needs of a particular enterprise. A conceptual model for the strategic management of human resource potential development is proposed. It includes defining strategic objectives, considering changes in the external environment, identifying prospective competency needs, assessing existing human resource potential, identifying competency gaps, selecting and implementing priority HR decisions, evaluating their effectiveness, and subsequent adjustment based on feedback. Digital HR tools are considered a cross-cutting means of information and analytical support for this management cycle. They facilitate competency assessment, HR analytics, employee learning and managerial decision-making. It is substantiated that digital technologies should not be regarded as an independent objective of HR policy, but as an instrument for improving the validity of HR decisions and aligning human resource potential with the strategic needs of the enterprise. The proposed approach supports the choice between employee development, reskilling, internal mobility and external recruitment based on identified competency gaps.

title: ОРГАНІЗАЦІЙНО-УПРАВЛІНСЬКІ МЕХАНІЗМИ АНТИКРИЗОВОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ ПІДПРИЄМСТВОМ В УМОВАХ ВОЄННИХ ВИКЛИКІВ
summary: The article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of enterprise anti-crisis management under wartime challenges, high uncertainty, and transformation of the external environment. The necessity of shifting from predominantly reactive responses to crisis phenomena toward a continuous preventive system of strategic management integrated with risk management, scenario forecasting, digital transformation, and business continuity management is substantiated. Based on a critical analysis of contemporary scientific approaches, the content of the concept of “enterprise anti-crisis management” is clarified, the main factors determining its effectiveness are systematized, and the relationship between strategic and tactical objectives at different stages of crisis development is determined. The authors propose a methodology for implementing an enterprise anti-crisis strategic planning system, which involves a consistent sequence of setting goals and objectives, developing an information and analytical base, conducting comprehensive crisis diagnostics, assessing risks, identifying priorities for anti-crisis measures, scenario modelling, implementing management measures, monitoring, and adjusting managerial decisions. Unlike the traditional financial approach, the proposed methodology provides for a comprehensive assessment of the financial, production, human resources, logistics, information, and organizational parameters of enterprise activity. The expediency of integrating the international standards ISO 22301, ISO 31000, and ISO/IEC 27001 into the anti-crisis management system is substantiated to ensure business continuity, effective risk management, and protection of information assets. The priority areas of anti-crisis measures are identified, including ensuring resource and energy resilience, diversifying supply sources and logistics routes, strengthening physical and cybersecurity, optimizing financial resources, adapting the business model, and continuously monitoring the effectiveness of managerial decisions.

title: The imprint of history: family firm origin and accounting information comparability in China
summary: Purpose Accounting information, serving as an important signal in capital markets, increasingly highlights the quality of financial reporting. This paper examines the differences in accounting information comparability across different family firm origins. Design/methodology/approach Using data on Chinese manufacturing family firms from 2009 to 2023, we employ a model with year and industry fixed effects to examine the relationship between family firm origin and accounting information comparability, as well as the underlying mechanisms. The final sample consists of 4,075 firm-year observations from 881 firms, with financial data obtained from the China Stock Market & Accounting Research database. Findings The main effects show that restructured family firms tend to have lower accounting comparability. The moderating effects show that the agency problem exacerbates this divergence in accounting comparability, whereas the number of generations involved in management mitigates it. The mechanism analysis shows that restructured family firms exhibit lower internal control quality and greater managerial myopia, both of which are associated with lower accounting comparability. Originality/value First, drawing on imprinting theory, this study finds that restructured family firms exhibit lower comparability of accounting information. This expands the scope of comparability research by extending it to factors related to historical origins. Second, this study expands upon the concepts of imprint dynamics and imprint decay in family firm origin research, thereby incorporating perspectives on the persistence and decay of imprints within imprinting theory. Finally, this paper adds a new dimension to research on the economic consequences of privatization for Chinese firms. Privatization not only affects operational efficiency but also shapes the information environment of financial reporting over the long term.

title: How do sustainability capabilities create retail performance over time? dynamic evidence from U.S. and Chinese retailers
summary: This study examines how sustainability-oriented technological innovation, sustainable supply chain management, and corporate social responsibility relate to environmental and manager-reported organisational performance in retail firms over time. Drawing on the natural resource-based view, institutional theory, and stakeholder theory, the study analyses a 12-wave monthly panel of 2410 retailers in the United States and China, comprising 26,998 firm-month observations. A multi-group hierarchical Bayesian continuous-time dynamic structural equation model estimates within-firm relationships, effects over one-, three-, and six-month intervals, time-varying mediation, and country differences. Technological innovation predicts environmental performance in both countries, but it strengthens sustainable supply chain management only in China. Sustainable supply chain management predicts organisational performance in both countries. Corporate social responsibility predicts environmental performance in both countries, while its direct short-run organisational effect is positive in the United States and negative in China. Environmental performance converts into organisational performance, and all three proposed indirect effects emerge, only in China during the focal six-month window. Exploratory analysis identifies integration-driven accelerators, evidence-driven pragmatists, and weakly-coupled drifters. The findings characterise retail sustainability as a dynamic conversion system with country-specific pathways to environmental and organisational outcomes; implications for individual customer responses require separate empirical testing.

title: Evaluating the impact of Lean 4.0 on operational excellence and sustainable performance of Indian automotive manufacturing industry: a PLS-SEM approach
summary: Purpose This study investigates the role of Lean 4.0 in operational excellence and sustainability within Indian automotive manufacturing units. This study aims to establish how the digital technologies of Industry 4.0 integrate with lean manufacturing tools to enhance operational performance and the triple bottom line of sustainability while exhibiting the mediating role of operational excellence. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods research design was adopted. A structured questionnaire was administered across multiple Indian automotive firms, and 198 valid responses from mid-to-large automotive component and original equipment manufacturers in India were selected for analysis. Partial least squares structural equation modeling via SmartPLS 4.0 was used to evaluate the hypothesized relationships between Lean 4.0, operational excellence and sustainability outcomes. To enhance external validity, a case study was conducted at a Pune, Maharashtra, India-based leading automotive supplier (Tier-1), providing qualitative insights and triangulation with the model’s empirical findings. Findings The findings reveal a significant positive impact of Lean 4.0 on both operational excellence and sustainability. Moreover, the relationship between Lean 4.0 and sustainability is somewhat mediated by operational excellence, but these effects are greatly moderated by organizational characteristics including leadership support and digital readiness. A case study demonstrates observable enhancements such as shorter cycle times, increased equipment efficiency and energy savings. Practical implications This study emphasizes how crucial it is to strategically match digital transformation with lean approaches to promote sustainable performance as well as production efficiency. Manufacturers can use the information to help with workforce preparedness, technology adoption and policymaking. The information also helps business and government organizations create incentives and support structures for the implementation of digital-lean practices. Originality/value This innovative study shows how Lean 4.0 methods relate to sustainability and operational excellence in the Indian automobile industry. It is supported by both a real-world case study and sophisticated statistical modeling.
